prs.title: test: GPU tests honour WGPU_BACKEND, so they run on Windows with an Intel GPU (#4)
prs.body:
I ran into this while working on #8974 (the #8764 Smart Filters fix): the targeted tests passed, but running the full suite locally before opening that PR crashed every time on my laptop.

On Windows with an Intel GPU, `cargo test` crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` in the first GPU test (e.g. ui-egui's `background_redraw` tests, then `adjust_preview_gpu`). It's the Intel Vulkan driver crash from #4: the app leaves Vulkan out on Intel, but the tests use wgpu's defaults, and creating an instance with Vulkan in it loads `igvk64.dll`.

`WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` avoids it for the kittest harnesses (egui reads it), but seven tests and four benches build their own instance with `wgpu::Instance::default()`, which takes every backend and ignores the environment, so they still crashed.

## Change

- Those 11 sites use `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle_from_env()`: the same defaults as `Instance::default()` plus `WGPU_BACKEND` and the other `WGPU_*` overrides. Where nothing is set (CI) nothing changes. This is what `parity.rs`'s own `gpu()` helper already does; these were the sites that didn't.
- `docs/development.md` (`WGPU_BACKEND` row) and the driver notes in `testkit/src/gpu.rs` say to run tests with `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` on Intel Windows machines.

## Results

Intel UHD Graphics 620, driver 27.20.100.9664, Windows 11:

| | before | after, `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` | access violation | 3712 passed |
| `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --test it` | access violation (`adjust_preview_gpu`) | 130 passed |
| `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test it` | access violation | 83 passed, 4 failed (below) |

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p photocraft-gpu -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

## Found along the way (not changed here)

On this GPU over DX12, four `parity` tests fail in **paged** mode with garbage GPU values, not small differences:
`documents_larger_than_the_texture_limit`, `growing_layer_keeps_its_resident_tiles`, `pages_are_evicted_under_the_budget`, `shared_tiles_upload_once_and_copy`. For example:

    viewport (paged): max diff inf/255 at (442,516): cpu [0.516, 0.700, 0.313, 1.0] gpu [2948133000000.0, -0.214, -0.043, 2.75e31]

They couldn't run here before (Vulkan crashed first). The driver is from 2021, so this may be a driver bug, but since the app uses DX12 on Intel by default it could affect large documents on Intel laptops. I can open a separate issue, and test again after a driver update, if that helps.

Possible follow-up: tests could pick DX12 + GL on Intel Windows automatically, as `gpu_startup::windows_auto_backends` does for the app, instead of relying on `WGPU_BACKEND`. Happy to do that if you'd like it.

prs.title: fix(xtask): reject unknown performance benchmark selections
prs.body:
## Summary

`cargo xtask perf --bench <typo>` silently filtered out every benchmark, returned success and could update the baseline without taking any measurements. Requested names were never checked against the declared benchmarks.

```diff
 perf --bench does-not-exist --update-baseline
- succeeds without measuring and writes an empty baseline
+ reports the unknown name before any build or output write
```

Validate every requested `--bench` name against `perf/budgets.toml` before planning the run. This also catches mixed valid/invalid selections. Known benchmarks skipped by quick mode or missing source requirements keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Before: the actual command exited 0 with no benchmarks, both with `--reuse` and with `--skip-build`. The new regression expected an error but got `Ok(())`; its temporary baseline was overwritten.
- After: all 68 xtask tests pass. The regression exercises `perf::run` in full and quick modes and checks that the baseline stays unchanged.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`: 31 crates, no violations.
- CLI checks reject unknown-only and mixed selections without changing reports or baseline. A known benchmark without quick arguments remains accepted in quick mode.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** benchmark-tooling

Only xtask argument validation and its documentation change. No dependencies or performance measurements change.

prs.title: fix(xtask): reject leading zeroes in numeric prerelease identifiers
prs.body:
## Summary

`cargo xtask version set 1.0.0-01` accepted an invalid numeric prerelease identifier, wrote it into the workspace manifest, then failed when Cargo parsed that manifest. The prerelease validator checked allowed characters but omitted the numeric leading-zero rule.

```diff
 version set 1.0.0-01
- writes an invalid Cargo.toml before Cargo rejects it
+ returns a validation error before writing
```

Reject numeric identifiers such as `01`, including after a dot. Keep valid identifiers such as `0`, `rc.0`, `01a` and `01-2`.

## Evidence

- Before: the new regression test failed with `validator accepted invalid version 1.0.0-01`. Cargo independently rejected temporary manifests with `invalid leading zero in pre-release identifier`.
- After: all 68 xtask tests pass, including the regression.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`: 31 crates, no violations.
- CLI checks for `1.0.0-01`, `1.0.0-rc.01` and `1.0.0-00.1` return errors and leave both Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock byte-for-byte unchanged.

- Final review: Grok 4.7 with high reasoning effort reported no blocking findings.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** release-tooling

Only xtask version validation changes. No dependencies or product crates change.

prs.title: feat(algo): describe the Gaussian blur as data for other devices
prs.body:
Part of #5772 (Phase 1, step 1.1 of [the plan](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/5772#issuecomment-6363558247)): the CPU side of the GPU blur operator. Independent of the Phase 0 PRs (#8848, #8852, #8859).

## Why
Phase 1 runs Gaussian Blur previews on the GPU as a compositor *layer operator*. The GPU must blur exactly as the CPU does: the same kernel weights or box widths, the same reach and the same edge behaviour. The CPU stays the oracle for parity tests and the fallback, and it applies OK. This PR makes that a single source of truth rather than two copies kept in step by hand.

## Change (`crates/algo`, new `separable.rs`)
- **`Separable`**: the blur as data. It holds either `Kernel(weights)` (radius ≤ 4) or `Boxes(widths)` (above 4), taken from `blur.rs`'s own `gaussian_kernel` and `box_widths`. `reach()` says how far an output pixel reads.
- **The CPU Gaussian is now built from it.** `blur::gaussian` picks its passes from `Separable::of`, so a change to the kernel (for example #8770's small-radius fix) reaches the GPU automatically. Behaviour is unchanged.
- **`OperatorRegion { reach, extent }`** is the region rule: `input(out)` gives the source pixels an output area reads. That is the area grown by the reach, inside the extent; beyond the extent the edge repeats.
- **`edge_extent(canvas, content)`** is the edge-repeat extent the engine already used for layer filters (canvas ∪ layer content). `engine/src/filters.rs` now calls it, so the CPU and the GPU operator share it.

## Tests
- `the_description_is_the_cpus_blur`, for radii 0.01, 0.3, 0.8, 2, 4, 4.5, 12, 40 and 250, checks that:
  - each radius uses the CPU's kernel or box widths;
  - kernels are normalised and odd-length, and box widths are odd;
  - the reach never exceeds the CPU's own halo.
- `an_impulse_spreads_no_further_than_the_reach` blurs one opaque pixel on the CPU at each radius and checks that nothing spreads past the reach. The exact kernel spreads exactly that far.

  One finding along the way: past the reach, the box passes' running sums leave float residue of around 1e-8. That is far below a 16-bit level, so it's ignored, and the comment says so.
- `output_depends_only_on_the_input_region` replaces every pixel outside `input(out)` with other noise and gets the same blurred output. It covers areas in the middle and at both canvas corners, where the edge repeats.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`: all pass (640 + 2,090 + 267 + …)
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-algo -p photocraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: clean

## Next in Phase 1
The GPU operator itself, in `crates/gpu`, with GPU-vs-CPU parity tests against this description.

The investigation for that step changed three details of the plan:
- **Fragment ping-pong passes, as the layer-effect maps already use, rather than compute.** The compositor has no compute pipelines, and fragment passes keep GL in reach.
- **The planner must know the operator's grown bounds,** because its clipping and occlusion use the layer's unblurred bounds.
- **Operator fingerprints are folded into the stack-prefix comparison,** which today compares only the `Document`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The tests check the kernel and box choice per radius, that an impulse spreads no further than the reach, and that output depends only on the input region. All checks are green. Approving.

prs.title: fix(plugins): bound a run's total plug-in memory, not just each instance
prs.body:
A filter run gives each band a fresh wasmi instance capped at 512 MiB of linear memory, and ran one band per rayon worker. The cap was therefore per instance times the thread count: one run on a 16-thread machine could hold about 8 GiB, and a plug-in smart filter repeated that on every re-render.

Limits gains max_total_memory_bytes (default 2 GiB), the budget for all of one run's instances together, and Limits::parallel_bands(threads), which allows only as many concurrent bands as max_memory_bytes fits into that budget (at least one). Plugin::apply uses it to size its groups of parallel bands, so with the defaults a run holds at most four instances at the cap however many cores there are. Plug-ins configured with a smaller per-instance cap keep every worker busy. The limit is listed in docs/plugins.md.

Tests (crates/plugins/tests/abi.rs):
- parallel_bands_fit_the_total_memory_budget: 16 workers with the default limits run 4 bands at once, not 16 (failed before: 16 != 4).
- one_band_at_a_time_matches_parallel_bands: a budget that holds one instance still covers every band on an 8-thread pool, with the same pixels as parallel bands.

Fixes #8603

approval.body: Read the non-test source: the total-memory limit and parallel_bands cap bound how many plug-in bands run at once, and the arithmetic is saturating. CI is green (tests on Ubuntu and Windows, Sonar). Approving.

prs.title: Box-filter minified patterns in the CPU and GPU samplers (#8831)
prs.body:
Fixes #8831.

Below 100 % a pattern tile was sampled with one bilinear tap per document pixel, so a shrunk tile aliased into full-contrast stripes and moiré. Now each pixel averages an `n × n` grid of bilinear taps spread over its footprint, with `n = ceil(1 / scale)` capped at 8. That box-filters the tile at the minification ratio. At 100 % and above `n` is 1 and the old single-tap code runs unchanged, so integer placements stay byte-exact (`identity_placement_tiles_exactly` and the overlay tests still pass as they are).

- **CPU** (`crates/compose/src/pattern.rs`): the bilinear tap moves into `Tile::sample_premul`, and `Tile::sample` becomes that tap plus unpremultiply. The new `Tile::sample_area(place, x, y)` averages the taps in premultiplied space, then unpremultiplies. `pattern::render` uses it, and so do the two direct sampling loops in `effects.rs` (pattern paint for Pattern Overlay and pattern strokes, and the bevel texture). Every entry point the issue lists goes through one of these: pattern fill layers, Pattern Overlay, pattern strokes, `edit.fill` and the Paint Bucket with a pattern, and the Pattern Stamp.
- **GPU** (`crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl`): `pattern_sample` mirrors this. The bilinear tap is now `pattern_tap`, and `pattern_sample` averages the same tap grid with the same cap and offsets, so it stays pixel-identical to the CPU. Pattern paints and the bevel texture both call it.

Tests:
- `pattern::tests::minified_pattern_is_filtered_not_aliased`: 1 px black/white stripes at 25 %, with a phase that puts every pixel centre on a white tile pixel. One tap returns pure white, which the test checks first. The filtered result is about 0.5, the local mean. The 100 % case of the same tile stays exactly 0 / 1.
- `gpu` parity `pattern_fill_layers` gets a 30 % case (`n = 4`), on top of the existing 70 % case, so the WGSL tap grid is checked against the CPU.

prs.title: fix(io): read linked smart objects for PSD export as regular files only
prs.body:
Saving a PSD embeds the file a linked smart object names, and it read that file with a bare std::fs::read. A link that names a FIFO blocked the save forever (opening a FIFO for reading waits for a writer), and one that names a device such as /dev/zero read until memory ran out. Every other linked-file read already goes through photocraft_format::read_file, which opens without blocking, refuses anything that is not a regular file and reads in bounded chunks; the PSD exporter now uses it too. Such a layer is written as pixels with a warning that says why, as for any other unreadable link.

The new test psd_export::tests::a_linked_fifo_is_not_read exports a document whose linked smart object points at a FIFO. Before the fix the export never returned (the test times out after 30 s); now it finishes and warns that the path is not a regular file.

Fixes #8601

prs.title: Select and Mask: Photoshop's full-window workspace (#7069, #8148)
prs.body:
Select › Select and Mask… now opens a full-window workspace laid out like Photoshop's, replacing the parameter dialog.

- **Options bar:** the current tool, Add/Subtract, Size, Hardness (Brush), Sample All Layers, Select Subject, and Refine Hair (greyed out, with a tooltip saying why: #2671).
- **Tools:** Quick Selection (W), Refine Edge Brush (R), Brush (B), Object Selection (W), Lasso and Polygonal Lasso sharing one slot (L), Hand (H), Zoom (Z). Shift+W and Shift+L cycle the shared slots.
- **View:** the document under its tab, shown in the chosen view mode. The view keys work as in the old dialog: O M V A T K Y, F cycles, hold X for the original image.
- **Properties:** Remember Settings; View Mode (views with their letters, Show Edge J, Show Original P, Real-Time Refinement, High Quality Preview, Transparency/Opacity, Overlay colour and Indicates); Refine Mode (Object Aware greyed out: #2788); Edge Detection; Global Refinements with Clear Selection and Invert; Output Settings; Reset, OK, Cancel.

The tools record `select.refineEdge` `edits`, and the Refine Edge Brush records `refineStrokes`. OK applies them as one history step, Cancel drops everything, and Ctrl+Z undoes one edit at a time. The preview runs in the background on a reduced copy (full size with High Quality Preview). It reuses the selection after the edits it has already applied, so a new stroke only costs that stroke. With Real-Time Refinement, the stroke being drawn joins the preview while the pointer moves. A targeted layer mask is refined and output to the mask. The control channel drives the workspace through `select.selectAndMask {"ui": {…}}` (documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`).

prs.title: ui: larger Align icons and overflow button; Save for Web keeps its width on an invalid Matte
prs.body:
Fixes three small UI problems. Each is a one- or two-line change.

**Align icons (#8849).** The Move tool's align buttons drew their glyph at 52% of the 24 px box (12 px), so they were hard to read next to the other options-bar controls. They now use a 16 px glyph in the same 24 px box (`icons::button_with_icon_size`).

**Document overflow button (#8834).** The `»` button at the end of the tab strip was a 12 px glyph in the dim text colour. It is now 16 px in the normal text colour, so it is easier to find. `overflow_button` is shared by the document and panel tab strips, so both get it.

**Save for Web, PNG-8 Matte (#8830).** Emptying or mistyping the Matte field made the whole dialog jump wider. The preview then fails with `matte is "none" or "#rrggbb"`, and `web_pane` drew that error as a label *beside* the pane in the row of previews, which pushed the pane over and made the resizable dialog grow to its maximum width. The same message is already shown on the row above the panes, so the pane no longer draws it.

Before/after (PNG-8, Matte emptied, 1300x800 window): the dialog was 1260 px wide and now stays at 970 px. The error line above the panes is unchanged.

**Not changed:** #8853 (eye icon of hidden layers). Photoshop leaves the eye column empty for a hidden layer, so the current behaviour matches it.

**Testing:** `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- align_bar tab_strip tabs_tests file_ui web_` (69 passed), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and offscreen `snapshot` renders before and after each change. UI only; no commands, layering or wasm changes.

Refs #8849, #8834, #8830

prs.title: Type: Roman Hanging Punctuation (trailing marks hang, don't steer the alignment)
prs.body:
## Summary

Photoshop's Paragraph panel checkbox **Roman Hanging Punctuation**, per paragraph style:

- **Layout** (`crates/text/src/layout.rs`): a trailing run of closing marks (`. , : ; ! ?` and their fullwidth twins `，．：；！？` plus `…`) trims out of the aligned width on center/right lines. A centered line ending in an ellipsis keeps its *text* centered and lets the marks hang past the anchor/box edge instead of pulling everything left; right-aligned content stays flush. A wrapped row of nothing but marks steps back onto the line above (merge-back): contiguous text ranges, the mark's glyphs on the merged row's baseline with manual kerning, the row range extended so carets and selection follow; known gaps: no optical kerning/decorations inside merged runs, no RTL, no vertical type (that's Burasagari's field).
- **Doc**: `ParagraphStyle.hanging: bool`, serde default off — `.pcraft` round-trips automatically; `format` needs no edits.
- **PSD**: `/Hanging` bool in the paragraph sheet, written right after `/LeadingType` as Photoshop's own writer places it (verified against the corpus files, which all carry `/Hanging false`); reading defaults off. Unknown PSD blocks stay verbatim.
- **Engine**: `type.setStyle` takes `"hanging":bool` (params doc updated); the report exposes the style.
- **UI**: checkbox at the bottom of the Paragraph section (Photoshop's place), a row in the Paragraph Styles editor, and the Character dock group grows one row (270→306) so the checkbox fits without scrolling; label translated in all 20 catalogs.
- `perturbed_para` style-mutation fuzzing covers the new field.

## Tests

- `crates/text/src/tests.rs`: `hanging_marks_do_not_steer_the_alignment` (centered point text keeps its content centered, right stays flush), `a_hanging_run_steps_back_onto_the_line_above` (merge-back: 2 rows → 1, mark past the box edge, caret on the merged row), `hanging_leaves_plain_paragraphs_untouched`, plus the engine-data write test `/Hanging true|false`.
- `crates/io/tests/psd_style_sheets.rs`: `hanging_punctuation_comes_from_the_paragraph_sheet` (sheet key read, missing key → off).
- `crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs`: `set_style_paragraph_hanging_round_trips` (on, off, junk value ignored like a junk `align`).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool_tests.rs`: `character_panel_hanging_checkbox_toggles_the_paragraph_style` (toggles both selected layers, untouched elsewhere, checkbox shows the state).

## Gates

`cargo test` on doc/text/engine/io/ui-egui green (175/1898/281+/3242 tests), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask wasm`, `cargo xtask layers`, `panic_hunt` (adversarial `type.setStyle` params) green, i18n gate green (20/20 catalogs), `cargo xtask scorecard` regenerated (`TYPE-218-10` done), snapshot-verified visually (panel checkbox checked, centered demo).

**Review fix, 25 October 2026 (86402460):** closed outlines retain their original shared boundary if fitting reverses winding or removes more than half their area. New regressions use real island chains at low fidelity.

### What's here
- `cutout/edges.rs`, step 4: the cracks between regions linked into chains from junction to junction (or closed loops round islands), each crack point moved along its normal to where the anti-aliasing puts the edge, with the regions on either side of each chain.

Two regions share one open chain between junctions, and every crack is in exactly one chain; an island is one closed chain; an anti-aliased edge lands mid-pixel; Douglas–Peucker keeps only an L's corner; a square keeps its corners and straight sides; a rounded corner is squared back; open chains keep their ends at every fidelity; curves pass through their vertices.

prs.title: Transform: remember selected interpolation (#8067)
prs.body:
Fixes #8067

## Problem
Transform sessions did not consistently reuse the selected interpolation. The earlier fix routed the Transform selection through Preferences > General > Image Interpolation, which Image Size and Crop also read, so changing Transform unexpectedly changed their default.

## Change
Transform now remembers its interpolation in saved tool options. Until the user chooses a Transform-specific mode, sessions inherit General's interpolation. Once selected, Transform reuses that choice across transform entry points and app restarts without changing the General preference. Regression tests cover reuse, persistence, and leaving the global preference unchanged.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -j 12 -- --test-threads=8` — 3,342 unit tests passed, 13 ignored; all integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -j 12 -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `cargo xtask wasm` — passed; reports three existing engine dead-code warnings for wasm.

prs.title: Compose: Extend Softer outer glows past Size (#7899)
prs.body:
## Problem

#7899 reports that a Softer Outer Glow falls to zero at `Size`, while Photoshop keeps a short fading tail. The current two-box tent has finite support, which causes the hard cutoff.

## Change

- Preserve the existing tent profile and add a short, range-scaled tail only to Softer outer glows.
- Derive the tail from the shape's Euclidean outside-distance field, max-combine it with the existing blur, and include its support in CPU effect margins.
- Use the same tail stage in the GPU compositor. Inner glows and Precise glows are unchanged.

Reference comparison from the issue: [Photoshop vs PhotoCraft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96cdaebe-4752-47af-b51e-de41d8adea8f).

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
- `cargo test -j12 -p photocraft-compose --lib softer_outer_glow` — 2 passed.
- `cargo test -j12 -p photocraft-gpu --lib softer_outer_glow` — 1 passed.
- `cargo test -j12 -p photocraft-gpu --test parity layer_effects_every_kind -- --nocapture` — passed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-gpu shader_validates` — passed.
- `cargo clippy -j12 -p photocraft-compose -p photocraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- `cargo xtask layers` — passed.
- `cargo xtask perf --quick` — passed; comparison against the recorded baseline was skipped because it was captured on a different machine class.
- `cargo test --release -j12 -p photocraft-io --features corpus,heif --test corpus psd_tools_import_flatten_oracle -- --nocapture` — passed; `layer_effects.psd` matched with no bad pixels.

The full `cargo xtask test-corpus` run could not be completed locally: available memory fell below 8 GiB during release compilation, so I stopped it to avoid further memory pressure. CI will run the full corpus suite.

Fixes #7899

The added Softer outer-glow tail is the same smoothstep falloff in both paths: `softer_glow_tail_width` and `softer_glow_tail_amplitude` are shared, the CPU adds it with `max` over the blurred coverage before the contour/finish step, and the GPU does the same through a new MGlow tail mode (selected by `p0.w`, which the existing glow call leaves at 0) followed by an MFinish max (`p0.x > 1.5`; the old 0/1 values behave as before). `margin()` and the GPU field reach are grown by the tail width, so the tail isn't clipped, and the width is capped at 6 px so large sizes stay local. prs.title: Filter Gallery › Cutout 4/4: trace the image into flat paper shapes
prs.body:
> **Part 4 of 4.** On review this was split into a stack, one stage per PR:
> 1. #8191 colour and palette
> 2. #8192 regions
> 3. #8193 edges and curves
> 4. this PR: the fill stage (`cutout/fill.rs`), `trace` / `render`, and the Filter Gallery hookup in `artistic_fx.rs`
>
> This branch contains the three earlier commits, so please review the fill/hookup commit 1d09845c and the island-preservation follow-up 5c306990. The original file split moved the code without changing it: `render` hashes over 54 input and setting combinations match the single-file version (2e95bf5). The description below is of the filter as a whole.

**Review fix, 25 October 2026 (5c306990):** closed outlines retain their original shared boundary if fitting reverses winding or removes more than half their area. New regressions use real island chains at low fidelity. Rendered-tone and empty-image regressions are included. The original 54-case hash comparison below applies to the file split before this intentional output correction.

### Problem
Cutout blurred the image and posterized each channel per pixel. Photo noise survived as speckle, edges were ragged, colours banded (inventing greens and teals), every shape got a dark halo, and Edge Fidelity did almost nothing.

### Solution
Cutout now traces the image into shapes and fills them back in as flat paper (new `crates/algo/src/cutout/` module, one file per stage):

1. **Smooth** within tones, edges kept: a bilateral filter (Tomasi & Manduchi 1998) in Oklab.
2. **Palette** of the picture's own colours: median cut + k-means (the existing `quantize` helpers, now crate-visible). A tone made of two clearly different hues splits in two; colours only noise apart merge.
3. **Regions**: 4-connected areas of one colour. Regions under the Edge Simplicity area, and slivers, merge smallest first into the neighbour they share most border with.
4. **Edges**: cracks are linked into chains between junctions, and each crack is moved to where the anti-aliasing on either side puts the edge (sub-pixel). Each chain is fitted once, so neighbouring shapes share one edge.
5. **Curves**: sharp bends stay corners (squared back where the pixels rounded them); runs are simplified (Douglas–Peucker) and drawn as Catmull-Rom curves. **Edge Fidelity** sets how closely outlines follow the image: rounded and loose at 1, tight at 3.
6. **Fill**: exact-area scan conversion, so edges are anti-aliased and the coverages of shapes that share an edge sum to one (no seams).
7. **Colour**: each shape keeps its region's lightness (stretched towards black and white) with the hue and colour strength of its own pixels nearby, so colour can drift gently inside a shape without crossing a cut.

**Tiling.** A trace is whole-image work, so a Filter Gallery stack containing a Cutout now declares `Halo::Bounds` and is prepared once before tiling (`artistic_fx::Prepared`, in the same spirit as `shape_blur::Prepared` and the radial blur plan). Effects up to the last Cutout run over the whole image and it is traced; each tile then fills in the shapes and runs the effects after it. Results don't depend on the tiling.

Clean-room: built from the published techniques named above and observed behaviour; no proprietary code.

### Before / after
Defaults (4 levels, Edge Simplicity 4, Edge Fidelity 2). Public-domain artwork (Vermeer; NASA *Earthrise*).

![Cutout on Girl with a Pearl Earring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andeecollard/photocraft/pr-assets/filter-gallery/cutout-girl.png)
![Cutout on Earthrise](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andeecollard/photocraft/pr-assets/filter-gallery/cutout-earth.png)

### Tests
- `cutout::tests`: exact square coverage; shapes cover every pixel exactly once (no seams) at two fidelities; filling is tile-independent; noise merges and a speck survives or goes with Edge Simplicity; Edge Fidelity really changes outlines (the old code changed 0.5% / 2.8% of pixels between fidelities 1→2 / 2→3 on smooth shapes, now about 9% / 5%).
- `artistic_fx::tests`: flat shapes with 1–2 px anti-aliased edges, a ramp becomes N steps, specks drop with simplicity, a stack around a Cutout is tile-independent; Cutout added to the every-slider-responds and tile-independence test. The existing all-filters test covers 8, 16 and 32-bit.
- Each stage also has its own unit tests in its PR.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-algo` (622 passed at the top of the stack), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt`, `xtask layers`, wasm check, `xtask scorecard --check`.

### Performance
24 MP, release, Apple Silicon (`bench_gallery`): Cutout ≈ 1.05 s (the old per-pixel posterize was 0.19 s). The trace runs once per apply; filling the tiles is a small part of it (≈ 35 ms over a 24 MP photo).

prs.title: fix(retouch): preserve Smudge pickup with live-pixel stroke commits
prs.body:
Pressure-sensitive Smudge strokes in #7281 can commit different pixels from replaying the recorded command: the reproduced 8-bit stroke differed in 7,635 channel values, by up to 47/255. Smudge carries a fixed-size pickup square, but the live path only supplied the current pressure-sized dab; the command working region also lacked the pickup padding.

This companion includes @wanikhawar’s #7281 unchanged plus one corrective commit. It gives live Smudge the complete pickup neighborhood, pads command replay consistently, and keeps writes inside the actual dab. The live-pixel release optimization remains intact.

### Review and landing order

Please review the combined result here before either PR lands. Once review and CI pass, merge #7281 first, then move only the corrective commit onto the resulting main, rerun validation and CI on that exact head, and merge this companion. Until then, this PR intentionally includes #7281’s changes as well as the fix.

Related work: #5804 addresses large-brush allocation/clipping separately; this PR fixes pickup correctness and does not claim to solve that issue.

### Validation

- Native build; 5,212 tests passed, 0 failed, 32 ignored across paint, engine and UI.
- Exact live/replay comparisons across all six sequential dab tools, pressure, elliptical tips, smoothing, scattering, transparency locks, selections, RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab and 8/16/32-bit; masks, alpha channels and Quick Mask; stale-document rejection.
- Independent padded paint oracle and actual canvas pen-input → release → journal replay → undo/redo regression.
- Strict Clippy, formatting, dependency layers, WASM (including HEIF check), registry panic hunt and quick performance gate passed.
- Same-machine release benchmark, 24 MP / 600 px Smudge: live release 0.2 → 0.2 ms; total measured live frames 134.5 → 134.0 ms. Correct fallback rendering costs 60.0 → 65.5 ms because it samples the full neighborhood. Small three-run benchmark; quick-gate baseline comparison skipped because its machine differs, and that gate has no retouch scenario.

Validated locally on macOS Apple Silicon. Physical tablet behavior and independent Photoshop fidelity remain unqualified; CI supplies the other platform checks.

prs.title: packaging: the portable zip holds the files, not a folder with the files in it
prs.body:
Fixes #7699.

`Compress-Archive -Path <folder>` archives the folder itself, so the portable zip contained

```
photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable\photocraft.exe
photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable\photocraft-cli.exe
photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable\portable.txt
...
```

rather than those files at its root. `<folder>\*` archives the contents.

Four things say the root is what was meant:

- this script's own synopsis — `photocraft-<version>-windows-<arch>-portable.zip   photocraft.exe + photocraft-cli.exe + portable.txt`;
- `portable.txt` ("While this file sits next to photocraft.exe…") and the advice to "copy the whole folder", which with a wrapper means the user's folder contains one more folder before the exe;
- VectorCraft's `packaging/windows/windows7.ps1`, which writes its portable zip with `Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $Stage '*')`;
- storytold/craft-launcher#627 — the launcher's portable install looked for the program at the archive root and found a wrapper folder instead. (That side now unwraps a single wrapper folder, so this is belt and braces; if you would rather keep the wrapper here, the launcher copes either way and the synopsis is what should change.)

Nothing read the layout back after writing it, which is how it drifted, so the three files are now checked inside the archive and the build fails loudly if they are not at its root.

### How this was checked

I have no Windows or PowerShell here, so I have not run `package.ps1`: the change copies the line that already works in `windows7.ps1`, and the check uses `Expand-Archive` + `Test-Path` + `throw` exactly as `sign.ps1` and this script use them. `packaging-lint` runs on this PR and is the static check; a maintainer running the packager on a Windows runner is the real one. No Rust is touched, so `cargo xtask ci` has nothing to say about it.

I read the whole diff (one hunk in `packaging/windows/package.ps1`) and, at the head, the rest of that script (how `$Portable`, `$TargetDir`, `$Dist` and `$Zip` are built, and `$ErrorActionPreference`), #7699 and the places that name the portable zip (`docs/releasing.md`, `docs/user/getting-started/install.md`, `README.md`). I haven't run PowerShell or the packager (no Windows runner here), so this is by my reading plus the hosted CI on this exact head, which is the static `packaging-lint`, not a packaging run.

**What I checked.**
- *The bug.* `$Portable` is a directory, so `Compress-Archive -Path $Portable` stores the folder as the top entry and the exe ends up one level down; #7699's report ("does not contain the expected executable at its root") is that. `-Path (Join-Path $Portable '*')` stores the folder's contents.
- *What the wildcard picks up.* `$Portable` is filled by the script with `*.exe`, `README.md`, the licence files, any `OFL-*.txt` fonts licences and `portable.txt`; there are no subfolders and no dot-files, so the wildcard doesn't miss anything that was archived before.
- *The check.* `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` is set at line 27, so a failing `Expand-Archive` stops the script; the three `Test-Path` checks `throw` with the zip path. `$Check` is under `$TargetDir\windows-package`, and it is deleted before the expand, so a leftover from a failed run (the `throw` skips the final `Remove-Item`) is cleaned up on the next run.
- *Docs.* The pages above only say to download and unzip the portable zip; none describes a wrapper folder, so nothing needs updating. The script's own synopsis says the zip holds the exe, the cli and `portable.txt`, which is now true.

I can't check that the packaging step on a Windows runner finishes and the zip opens as intended; a run of `package.ps1` on a Windows build would show it.

prs.title: Actions: a fractional setting an integer field cannot hold is refused, not rounded
prs.body:
Closes #7669 and #7670. **#7671 (Stroke) is not in this change** — see below.

`Kind::Long` wrote its param through `long()`, which rounds:

```rust
fn long(v: f64) -> D {
    D::Integer(v.round().clamp(f64::from(i32::MIN), f64::from(i32::MAX)) as i32)
}
```

Photoshop's field really is an integer, so a fractional setting cannot be written — but rounding it put a different edit in the file than the one recorded, with `skipped` empty and nothing to say so. Measured through `actions.save` and back:

| step | recorded | in the file | read back |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filter.pixelate.crystallize` | `cellSize: 5.4` | `ClSz 5` | `cellSize: 5` |
| `filter.distort.ripple` | `amount: 81.4` | `Amnt 81` | `amount: 81` |

(The first row is the new round-trip test run against `main`: `left: Some(5.0), right: Some(5.4)`.) The reports measure what that does to the pixels — 385 to 583 differing colour components at every bit depth.

### Why Stroke is out

`edit.stroke` normalises the width itself:

```rust
// crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs:137
let width = p.get("width").and_then(Value::as_f64).filter(|w| w.is_finite()).unwrap_or(1.0).clamp(1.0, 250.0).ceil() as usize;
```

`.ceil()`, so `width: 2.4` renders at **3** — an integer field can hold that exactly, and refusing the step would throw away something expressible. On `main` it renders at 3 and exports `Wdth 2` with `skipped` empty, which is wrong in both directions this PR could have gone. @PerchAnton's #7696 normalises it instead, which is the only approach that reproduces what the user saw. My first version refused it; that was my mistake.

### What changed

The refusal is a field's own kind, `Kind::LongExact`, carried by the two fields whose command uses the setting as written:

- Crystallize's `ClSz` — `cell_size: f(p, "cellSize", 10.0).clamp(3.0, 300.0)`, no rounding
- Ripple's `Amnt` — `amount: f(p, "amount", 100.0).clamp(-999.0, 999.0)`, no rounding

`long_exact` returns `None` for a value such a field cannot hold — a fraction, or a magnitude past `i32` — and `fields_to` passes that up. The step then takes the path a step with no Photoshop equivalent already takes: strict export names it and fails, `skipUnsupported: true` leaves it out and lists it in `skipped`.

The first version sent **all 26** `Kind::Long` fields through `long_exact` on the strength of three reports, one of which turned out to need the opposite. The other 24 keep `long()` until someone has read each against its command.

Refusing, rather than exporting a near miss, is what the rest of this file does: `pixel_target` already refuses a filter step aimed at a mask because "Photoshop's descriptor for a plain event has no field for a mask … so such a step can't be exported faithfully".

The strict error now reads "can't be written as a Photoshop step: it has no equivalent event, or a setting its event can't hold", since both cases arrive there.

### Tests

- `a_fractional_setting_an_integer_field_cannot_hold_is_refused_not_rounded` — both reported steps: strict export fails naming the step, `skipUnsupported` reports it in `skipped`. On `main` the first `unwrap_err` panics with `Ok(…)`.
- `whole_number_settings_for_integer_fields_still_round_trip` — the same with whole numbers, plus `edit.stroke`, which still exports: written, `skipped` empty, and every param read back as itself. Numbers compare by value and anything else as it is, so string settings (`size`, `color`, `location`) are checked rather than passing vacuously through `as_f64` on both sides.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 5 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm).

### Still to do here

@PerchAnton has offered their `atn_crystallize_cell_size.rs` and `atn_ripple_amount.rs` suites (four tests each) for this PR, with their authorship kept. Waiting on @echelon to confirm the order before moving them, per the discussion below.

### Not in this change

`long()` stays for the hand-written mappings that use it (`Lvls` input/output levels, `Thsh`, `Tlrn`, `Qlty`, `NCol`, `Dpth`, the Color Balance triples). Most take whole numbers from a range the command already clamps, and each is its own command scope; if you'd like them refused on the same footing, I'm happy to follow up.

approval.body:

The follow-up commits narrow the refusal per field and make the round-trip test compare string settings (`size`, `color`, `location`) as well as numbers, so the whole-number case is actually checked.

No defect found. CI is green at this head.

prs.title: Pen: Path Operations menu, as in Photoshop (#1397)
prs.body:
Closes #1397. Closes #7533.

The Pen, Freeform Pen and Curvature Pen get Photoshop's **Path Operations** button in the options bar, after the stroke controls. Its icon shows the current operation.

## Behavior

- **Menu:** New Layer, Combine Shapes, Subtract Front Shape, Intersect Shape Areas, Exclude Overlapping Shapes, then Merge Shape Components below a separator.
- **Shape mode:** New Layer (the default) keeps today's behavior, one shape layer per path. Any other operation adds the new path to the selected shape layer with that operation, so a hole can be cut in a shape (the mug handle in #7533). With no shape layer selected, a new one is started. One History step per path.
- **Path mode:** New Layer is disabled and the Pen combines. The operation is stored on the subpath added to a targeted vector mask, the selected path or the Work Path (before this, Path mode always combined). With no path selected, a new Work Path is started as before.
- **Merge Shape Components** bakes the operations into plain outlines. In Shape mode it runs the existing `layer.combineShapes.mergeShapeComponents`. In Path mode it runs a new engine command, `path.mergeShapeComponents` (work, saved or `layer` path, via `edit_path`). Both share the new `vector_cmds::bake_path`, which also keeps an inverted path inverted. The item is disabled with fewer than two components.
- **Agents:** `ui.set` accepts `penMode` (`path`/`shape`) and `penPathOp`. `ui.inspect` reports `toolOptions.pen_path_op`, and the MCP `ui_set` description lists both fields.
- **Settings:** the setting is `ToolOptions::pen_path_op` (serde default `newLayer`) and is part of the three Pens' Reset Tool / tool-preset keys. An unknown stored value falls back to New Layer.

- **Changing drawn components** (tester feedback): Path Selection now selects components (click; ⇧-click adds or removes one; a click off them deselects; a drag moves only the selected ones, with their anchors shown solid). It has the Path Operations menu too. With components selected, the menu changes their operation through a new engine command, `path.setOperation` (Work Path, saved path, shape layer or vector mask; one History step), and its icon shows that operation.
- **Keys:** `+` picks Combine Shapes and `-` picks Subtract Front Shape while a Pen tool or Path Selection is active, for the selected components and for the next path. Adobe Community threads report these as Photoshop's keys. Because `+` is ⇧= on a US layout, ⇧+ no longer steps the blend mode with these tools. It still does with the others.
- **Continuing an open path:** the Pen carries on an open path from its endpoint in Shape mode (the selected shape layer) and on a targeted vector mask. Before, it only did this on the Work Path and saved paths. Closing the open path that a stroke-only shape layer was made of gives the layer the options bar's fill and stroke, as if the path had been drawn closed.

## Assets and docs

- Six original icons, `assets/icons/path-op-*.svg`, drawn on Lucide's 24 px grid and stroke, with a row in `ATTRIBUTION.md`.
- The "Path operations" tooltip is translated in all 20 catalogs; the menu labels already were.
- `docs/ui-parity.md`: the row stays **partial**, because the Shape tools don't have the menu yet. `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the new `ui.set` fields.

## Not in this PR

- The same menu on the Shape tools.
- Keys for Intersect and Exclude: I couldn't find Photoshop's bindings for them.
- Merge works on the whole path, not only the selected components. Like the existing shape-layer command, its outlines are traced from coverage.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --lib --tests`, `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored`, `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests` (3091 lib tests), `cargo test -p photocraft-automation --tests`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: pass. `cargo xtask parity`: checklist unchanged (no new menu item).
- New tests:
  - `pen_path_ops_tests.rs`: hole cut in the selected shape layer and its undo; an operation with no shape layer selected; Path-mode operations on the work path, a saved path and a vector mask; the menu driven with kittest (New Layer disabled in Path mode, Merge); Merge disabled with one component; unknown-value fallback.
  - Engine `merge_shape_components_*` plus bad-param cases, and `ui_set_drives_the_pen_path_operation`.
- Checked visually in an offscreen snapshot and in the running desktop app.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The finding is fixed. `freeform_locked_shape` (`tools/vector_ui/pen.rs`) mirrors exactly when the append route would reach the engine's lock refusal: Shape mode, a Path Operation set, a selected shape, and `effective_locks(id)` with `all` or `pixels` (the same condition the engine checks in `shape.create` with `addTo`). `lasso_ui.rs` calls it on the Freeform Pen's press, when no stroke is active, and refuses the press before the drag starts: the status bar reads "Locked" as an error, and no drag is taken, so there is no stroke to lose and no History step. prs.title: fix(engine): guard trim and duplicate merged against documents exceeding render limits (#7223)
prs.body:
Fixes #7223

### Problem
`photocraft_compose::flatten` refuses to render canvas areas larger than `MAX_RENDER_PIXELS` (2^30 px) and returns an empty buffer to prevent allocation aborts. When `image.trim` or `image.duplicate {"mergedOnly": true}` was run on a document exceeding this limit (e.g. 40,000 × 30,000 px):
- `image.trim` with `basedOn: "topLeft"` panicked with an out-of-bounds index on `buf.px[0]`, and other modes reported a misleading "nothing to trim to".
- `image.duplicate {"mergedOnly": true}` passed the empty buffer to `Surface::write_region`, triggering an assertion failure panic on the data length.

### Solution
- In `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs:trim`, guarded against canvas bounds exceeding `photocraft_compose::MAX_RENDER_PIXELS` (or returning an empty buffer for non-empty canvas), returning `Err(EngineError::Other("the document is too large to trim".into()))`.
- In `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs:duplicate`, guarded `mergedOnly` against document bounds exceeding `photocraft_compose::MAX_RENDER_PIXELS`, returning `Err(EngineError::Other("the document is too large to duplicate merged".into()))`.
- Added regression unit test `trim_and_duplicate_merged_on_too_large_document_fail_gracefully_without_panic` in `image_cmds.rs` verifying both commands fail gracefully without panicking and preserve the document.

The shared render-limit helper checks the pixel budget and rejects empty flatten output before command mutation; the regression tests confirm document state, revision, and document count remain unchanged on failure. Exact-head CI passed with no unresolved review threads.

prs.title: Smart Filters: double-clicking a Liquify filter reopens it in the Liquify workspace
prs.body:
## What's wrong

Double-clicking a Liquify smart filter in the Layers panel opened the generic parameter form, whose only field is Mesh Size, instead of the Liquify workspace. `smart_ui::open_editor` sent Camera Raw and the Filter Gallery to their own dialogs, adjustments to their Image › Adjustments editors, and every other filter to `filter_dialog`. OK on that form replayed the recorded strokes on the form's mesh size. Filter › Liquify always opens with no strokes, so the recorded strokes could not be edited again.

To see it: make a smart object, run Filter › Liquify, drag one stroke, press OK, then double-click the Liquify row under Smart Filters.

## What changed

`main` has the first three items since #8577, which merged this pull request at its earlier head (cfa5242). The diff against `main` is now the fourth item and its test.

- `open_editor` sends a Liquify smart filter to a new `liquify_ui::open_smart_filter`.
- `open_smart_filter` opens the workspace on the smart object's pixels below that filter, with the filter's recorded strokes and mesh size, as `gallery_ui::open_smart_filter` does (#3426).
- OK then runs `layer.smartFilter.setParams` with the strokes and the mesh size in one history step, and no second Liquify filter is added. OK after Restore All leaves the filter with no strokes. Cancel leaves the filter unchanged. Filter › Liquify on a smart object still adds a new filter.
- `open_smart_filter` captures the filter with `smart_filter_dialog::target`, and OK checks it with `smart_filter_dialog::validate_target` before `setParams`, as the other Smart Filter editors do. When the document or the filter stack changed while the workspace was open, OK updates nothing and the status bar asks to reopen the dialog.

Ten-W reported this in #6571. Part of #6571: the Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp smart filters it also lists are left for later.

## Tests

Tests in `dialogs/liquify_ui/tests.rs` use a smart object with a Liquify filter (one stroke, mesh size 3) under a Gaussian Blur. The first three are in `main` with #8577:

- `smart_filter_double_click_edits_the_recorded_liquify` checks the workspace's strokes, mesh size and source pixels, then that a new stroke and OK update the filter in one step and Undo restores it. Without the new `open_editor` branch it fails at "no generic parameter form".

- `smart_filter_edit_after_the_stack_changed_updates_nothing` moves the Liquify filter below the blur while the workspace is open and checks that OK leaves both filters and the history unchanged. Without the `validate_target` check, OK reports no error and the test fails.

prs.body:
<!-- integration-refresh-20261025:start -->
**Latest integration checks (2026-10-25):** head `d744f155a07cb1703ef0da09c944e2054ccb1550` includes main `c65b5d25d3cfee71ecdb96b6549721e0deac8840` through a normal merge. Fixes #6426.

Automation accepts absolute paths using either the configured root spelling or its canonical spelling. Resolve the root once and keep I/O relative to its held directory capability. prs.title: Fail control startup promptly when its port is occupied
prs.body:
## Summary

Bind the control listener before GPU/display initialization, and pass the bound listener to the server. An occupied port now exits promptly with a useful diagnostic and status 2.

```text
control startup
  validate token and workspace
  bind 127.0.0.1:port → on failure: report error, exit 2
  initialize display/GPU
  start server with bound listener
```

Fixes #6428.

## Evidence

- **Before:** With its requested port held by another process, the desktop logged a bind error but remained running beyond a 10-second deadline.
  **After:** The rebuilt desktop exits promptly with status 2 and the bind diagnostic, without creating the GPU-startup marker.
- Added an occupied-port process regression with a bounded deadline, and a unit test that authenticates and dispatches through a prebound listener.
- Windows GNU: all 130 desktop unit tests and 5 startup integration tests passed. Strict all-target Clippy, formatting, layer checks, and all 24 WebAssembly checks passed for the combined local changes. Loopback tests ran outside the sandbox because it denies local socket access.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No data-format or dependency changes; the startup ordering can be reverted.

**Blast Radius:** startup

Control-enabled launches now fail before display initialization when the requested listener cannot bind.

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Read the whole diff at this head, and `main.rs` around it. The control setup (bind, token, workspace) now runs before the log file, single-instance handling and any display or GPU initialization, and an occupied port prints the bind error and exits 2. The bound listener travels in `control` into the app-creation closure and is handed to `control_server::start`, so the server no longer binds on its own. `--control` launches skip single-instance handling, so moving the setup ahead of it changes nothing there. The unit test authenticates and dispatches through a prebound listener, and the process test checks exit 2, the bind message, no GPU marker, and a 10 second bound. CI is green at this head.

One thing worth a quick check, not a blocker: the CPU-compatibility relaunch near the end of `main` spawns a new process with the same `--control <port>` after a renderer failure. That works only if the listener has been dropped by then, which holds if `control` is owned by the creator closure that `run_native` consumes on return (it is moved in the `if let Some((listener, token, _)) = control` and not used afterwards). If the child ever exits 2 with "failed to bind" after a GPU failure, that is the place to look.

prs.title: Hand tool: Cmd held zooms in and Alt zooms out, as in Photoshop
prs.body:
Fixes #6434.

The held-key tools in `hold_keys.rs` (from #275, with ⌥Space from #2877) cover Space, ⌘Space and ⌥Space, and ⌘ alone is the Move tool for the painting tools, but the Hand is rightly left out of that, so with the Hand selected ⌘ and ⌥ did nothing. This adds the Hand's own pair, as in Photoshop: ⌘ (Ctrl off the Mac) held is a temporary Zoom In, ⌥ (Alt) a Zoom Out, ⌘⌥ zooms out too, and the Hand is back when the key comes up. It goes through the same `Temporary` path as ⌘Space, so clicks, scrubby drags and the cursor all follow, and a bound key still wins. Two cases keep ⌘ for something else: an open Free Transform (its distort handles), and a modifier pressed in the middle of a Hand drag, which keeps panning instead of stopping the pan. A latched ⌥ from Window › Modifier Keys doesn't switch the Hand, same as ⌘ for the Move tool; happy to switch if you'd rather it did.

- `hold_keys::tests::cmd_and_alt_with_the_hand_tool_zoom_in_and_out_while_held`: fails on main (`held_tool` is `None` with ⌘ held, expected `ZoomIn`), passes here
- `hold_keys::tests::cmd_mid_pan_or_during_free_transform_is_not_the_hand_tools_zoom`: guards the mid-drag and Free Transform cases (fails if the mid-drag check is removed)
- `cmd_is_not_the_move_tool_for_selection_hand_zoom_pen_shape_or_type_tools` now expects Zoom In for the Hand, still never Move
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib hold_keys::tests::`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

prs.title: Video Frames to Layers: every page of a multi-page TIFF (part of #6379)
prs.body:
Part of #6379 (the multi-page TIFF part).

File › Import › Video Frames to Layers loads every frame of an animated GIF as its own layer, but a multi-page TIFF gave only its first page. `load_frames` (also behind Layer › Video Layers › New Video Layer from File) now takes every full-resolution page of a TIFF's main IFD chain, in file order, one layer (or frame) each:

prs.title: Windows releases ship a symbols zip: the release build's PDBs for profilers (#688)
prs.body:
Fixes #688.

Windows releases ship no PDBs, so a profile of the installed PhotoCraft (WPA, Superluminal) shows addresses instead of function names, and a PDB from a local rebuild of the same commit doesn't match the published exes. The release build already writes `photocraft.pdb` and `photocraft_cli.pdb` (the exes record them by bare file name), they just weren't packaged.

## Change
- `packaging/windows/package.ps1`: after the portable zip, copies both PDBs from the release build into `photocraft-<v>-windows-<arch>-symbols.zip` in `dist/release`, plus `symbols.txt`. It fails the packaging step if a PDB is missing rather than shipping a partial zip. Signing doesn't change the PDB signature an exe records, so the PDBs match the signed exes. The shared release workflow (`craft-common-actions` `release.yml` → `draft-release`) uploads everything in `dist/release` and adds it to `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so no workflow change is needed.
- `packaging/windows/symbols.txt` (new): which binaries they match, and how to load them (copy next to the exe, or add the folder in WPA / Superluminal / Visual Studio / `_NT_SYMBOL_PATH`).
- `docs/releasing.md`: the asset table and a short "Symbols zip" note.

The release profile has `debug = 0`, so these PDBs carry function names but no source line tables. That is what function-level flame graphs need. Line tables (`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only` for the Windows build) could follow if maintainers want them; I left the build settings alone. The PDB from my local release build is about 9.8 MB (2.3 MB zipped). macOS dSYMs and Linux debug files would be follow-ups in their own packaging scripts.

## Tests
There's no test harness for the packaging scripts. I ran these locally:
- PowerShell's parser on `package.ps1`: 0 errors.
- The new block on its own against a local `target/release`: it copied `photocraft.pdb` and `symbols.txt` and zipped them. It threw the intended error for the missing `photocraft_cli.pdb`, since I had only built the app.
- Checked that a release `photocraft.exe` records its PDB as just `photocraft.pdb`, so the shipped file names resolve.

I haven't run the full `package.ps1` (it needs WiX and signing). The release workflow will exercise it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: Shift+Alt+right-click opens Photoshop's HUD Color Picker (#6098)
prs.body:
## What

Implements the HUD Color Picker (#6098): with a painting tool, **Shift+Alt+right-click** on the canvas now opens Photoshop's floating hue strip + saturation/value square anchored under the pointer, instead of the Brush Preset picker.

- While the right button stays down, moving the pointer over the HUD sets the foreground colour live; releasing the button keeps the colour and closes the HUD.
- **Esc** restores the colour the gesture started from.
- The gesture's `tools.setColors` calls share one `coalesce` key, so the whole pick is one history step (Rule 1); nothing paints and no document edit happens.
- `brush_resize::is_right_gesture` now requires Shift *not* be held, so Alt+right-drag brush resize and the new Shift+Alt HUD gesture stay distinct. Plain right-click still opens the Brush Preset picker.
- Agents can drive it: `ui.pointer` with `"button": "right", "shift": true, "alt": true` (down opens, up closes).
- New module `crates/ui-egui/src/color_hud.rs` (drawn as meshes, hit-tested from the raw pointer, since egui widgets can't track a held right button); `UiState.color_hud` exposes it to the control channel; documented in `docs/color-picker.md`.

## Tests

- 7 new unit tests (open/gesture exclusivity, live pick + coalescing, release keeps, Esc restores, control channel, `pick_at` mapping, regressions for plain right-click and Alt+right-drag resize).
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`: 2933 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask layers`: OK.
- Rendered offscreen via the snapshot example and verified the hue strip/square geometry and clamping on screen.

Fixes #6098

prs.title: Fix painting workflows, File Info and layer selection
prs.body:
This change fixes nine painting and dialog workflows reported against PhotoCraft 0.9:

- File Info's Description, Keywords and Copyright fields accept multiple lines. Enter inserts a line break, and the scrollable form keeps its buttons accessible. Fixes #6116.
- Brush and Pencil offer Behind painting, preserving opaque pixels and compositing beneath translucent pixels in the document's native color channels. Fixes #6115.
- Eyedropper samples become grayscale foreground/background values when targeting a layer mask, Quick Mask or alpha channel. Fixes #6086.
- Holding Space during a Pen drag moves the anchor and both handles together; releasing Space resumes handle editing. Fixes #6084.
- The color picker accommodates longer translated action labels and translates its foreground/background title. Fixes #6109.
- The Move tool shows the platform copy cursor for Alt-drag duplication, retaining that cue until the active copy drag finishes. Fixes #6102.
- File Info uses Document Title, Copyright Notice and Copyright Info URL labels. Fixes #6125.
- File Info orders fields by the requested metadata workflow instead of alphabetically. Fixes #6126.
- An assignable Select Layer Under Cursor command selects the visible hit layer through rotated, flipped and zoomed views, preserving selection on misses and refusing changes during modal dialogs or strokes. Fixes #2298.

Regression coverage includes real keyboard/pointer interactions, metadata confirm/reopen and cancel, masks at 8/16/32-bit depth, native RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab Behind compositing, selection/transparency locks, live stroke composition, and undo/redo. All visual fixtures are generated locally from PhotoCraft's own UI and synthetic document contents.

Touched-crate clippy with warnings denied, formatting, layer checks, wasm checks and parity generation pass. File Info, German Color Picker and Behind painting were rendered and inspected.

prs.title: Marquee: Fixed Size selects exactly the entered width and height (fixes #6015)
prs.body:
Fixes #6015.

**Problem:** with the Rectangular (or Elliptical) Marquee set to Style › Fixed Size, the selection was one pixel larger on each side than the size entered: 10 × 10 selected 11 × 11, and 1 × 1 selected 2 × 2. The fixed rectangle starts at the press point, which usually sits between pixel edges (e.g. x = 50.4, so 50.4..60.4). `marquee_px` then floors the near edge and ceils the far edge, which gives 50..61. This is the same cause as #5472 for ⇧ squares.

**Fix:** `canvas::fixed_size_px` builds the Fixed Size rectangle on whole pixels: the near edge goes to the closest pixel edge and the far edge is exactly W × H away. Both the live outline and readout and the selection made on release use it, through `marquee_preview_px`. A click without a drag now places the Fixed Size selection, as in Photoshop. Before, a click deselected. Normal and Fixed Ratio are unchanged: a click still deselects.

**Tests:**
- `canvas::tests::fixed_size_px_is_exactly_the_size`: down-right and up-left, 1 × 1, fractional sizes.
- `marquee_tests::fixed_size_selects_exactly_the_entered_size`: through the real canvas, for both marquee tools and 10 × 10, 1 × 1 and 64 × 32. The press lands between pixels, then the test checks the readout, the dragged selection and a click.

**Checks run locally:** the marquee tests in `photocraft-ui-egui` (`fixed_size`, `marquee_styles`, `square_px`, `one_pixel`, `the_live_outline`), `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`. No new UI strings. CI covers the rest.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep detached documents in one interactive window
prs.body:
## Summary
- Keep a torn-off document active and remove it individually from the main tab strip and canvas.
- Mark Float All windows as floating and avoid reactivating a detached document on every focused frame.
- Route canvas input through the focused viewport.

## Reproduction
1. Open at least two documents.
2. Drag one document tab outside the tab strip to detach it into a floating OS window.
3. Check whether the document still appears in the main tab strip or canvas.
4. Focus the floating window and use a canvas tool.
5. Try Window > Arrange > Float All in Windows.

Expected: a torn-off document stays active in its floating window, is absent individually from the main tab strip and canvas, and canvas input is handled by the focused viewport. Float All creates floating document windows as well.

## Checks
- UI integration tests: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`, and `cargo build -p photocraft`: passed.
- The full UI unit suite has one known GPU precision failure on the AMD RX 5700 at F32 mip 5 (delta 5.96e-8); the floating-window regression tests pass.

Fixes #6277; related original request: #3733

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. A document torn off into its own window is now marked `floating` and the main canvas, tab strips and Arrange tiles skip it, so the same page is no longer drawn in both viewports. The main canvas falls back to the first docked document when the active one is floating, and stays blank (dots only) when every document is floating. Activation follows focus: a click in the main window only activates a tile or the fallback document while that viewport is focused, and a floating window activates its document once when it gains focus.

Tab handling stays consistent with the document list. Tab ids, close, context-menu and overflow actions use document indices, and `move_target_after_filter` maps a drop position in the docked-only strip back to the full list (checked against its two test cases). Floating the same document again reuses its open window rather than opening a second one, and a closed window can be floated again.

The tests cover the torn-off document in both themes, the Arrange layout with a floating document, tab reorder with a floating document in between, and the float, float-all and reuse behaviour. CI is green at 50b1f67. The branch has merge conflicts, so it needs a rebase before merging.

prs.title: Guides: ⌥ turns a dragged guide; dropping one on either ruler deletes it (#5034)
prs.body:
Fixes #5034.

## What changed

Two Photoshop guide behaviours:

- **⌥ (Alt) turns a guide while it's dragged.** This works whether the guide comes out of a ruler or an existing guide is dragged with the Move tool (or with ⌘ and another tool).
  - The guide turns between horizontal and vertical about the pointer, so out of the left ruler it comes out horizontal.
  - Letting go of ⌥ before the release turns it back.
  - An ⌥-click on a guide turns it in place.
- **Dropping a guide on either ruler deletes it, whichever way it runs.** Before, a horizontal guide dropped on the left ruler was still level with the image, so it only moved.

### Implementation

- **engine:** `view.moveGuide` takes an optional `toOrientation`. A turned guide is one undo step and keeps its colour, and a `%` position is of the new axis. A bad value, or `toOrientation` on another guide command, is refused without touching the guides.
- **ui (`rulers.rs`):**
  - `GuideDrag` keeps the guide's own orientation (so `index` still points into the right list), plus two new fields: `flipped` (⌥ held) and `over_ruler`.
  - `GuideDrag::track` follows the pointer for both drag paths, and `shows_vertical` is what's drawn and committed.
  - The rulers set `over_ruler` from the pointer each frame.
  - `finish_drag` creates, moves or turns the guide, or deletes it when it's dropped outside the canvas or on a ruler.
- **canvas.rs:** the Move-tool and ⌘ guide drags use `track` with ⌥.
- **docs/ui-parity.md:** new row and revision entry.

## How it was checked

- `cargo xtask ci` on macOS passes all 5 steps (fmt, clippy, test, layers, wasm).
- New tests:
  - `edit_cmds::tests::move_guide_turns_a_guide`: turn with `%` of the new axis, colour carried, one undo step each, bad params refused.
  - `rulers::tests::alt_turns_a_guide_dragged_out_of_a_ruler`: a real egui drag out of the left ruler with ⌥ held gives a horizontal guide at the pointer's y.
  - `rulers::tests::alt_turns_a_guide_moved_with_the_move_tool`: ⌥-drag turns the guide in one undo step, releasing ⌥ first keeps it vertical, and an ⌥-click turns it in place.
  - `rulers::tests::a_guide_dropped_on_either_ruler_is_deleted`: the pointer over the left or top ruler marks the drop and deletes a horizontal guide; over the canvas it moves.
- In the running app over `--control`:
  - Set up a 400×300 document with a vertical guide at x=200, then used `ui.pointer` with the Move tool: down on the guide, then move and up with `alt: true` at (120, 223).
  - History gained one "Move Guide" step.
  - The document saved through `app.save` has a horizontal guide at y=223 and no vertical one (read from the PSD's resource 1032).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. ⌥ while dragging a guide now turns it, as in Photoshop, and a guide dropped on either ruler is deleted.

- **Engine:** `view.moveGuide` takes `toOrientation`. A same-orientation value is a plain move, anything but "horizontal"/"vertical" is rejected, `view.newGuide` rejects the parameter, and a % position is resolved against the axis the guide ends up on. A turned guide is removed from one list and pushed to the other, and its colour is moved to the new axis. It is one history step.
- **UI:** `GuideDrag::track` recomputes `flipped` and `pos` from the pointer and the current ⌥ state on every press, move and release, so letting go of ⌥ before release turns it back. `finish_drag` checks the drop against the extent of the axis the guide is shown on, which avoids the cross-axis bounds problem. `over_ruler` comes from the previous frame's pointer position, and the comment says so.
- **Callers:** all `GuideDrag` literals now use `..Default::default()`.

The tests cover the engine command (colour, % axis, undo, bad params), a ruler drag with ⌥ held, the Move tool with ⌥ held, ⌥ released and ⌥-click, and drops on the left ruler, top ruler and canvas. CI is green at 4b1bd6f. The branch conflicts with main, so it needs a rebase.

prs.title: Shapes: independent fill and stroke paints (solid, gradient, pattern), part 1
prs.body:
Pattern fills on shape layers rendered as transparent, and the shape commands only kept part of a paint. Gradient opacity stops, midpoints, offset, dither and align, solid alpha or non-RGB colours, and pattern angle, phase and link were dropped or reset on the way through `shape.create`, `shape.edit` and `shape.info`.

This is the first part of splitting #3446. It changes only the rendering and engine side, with no UI changes:

- Pattern tiles and placement move from `photocraft-compose` into `photocraft-vector` (`photocraft_vector::pattern`, re-exported by compose). Sampling now handles non-finite and huge coordinates. A tile over 64 MiB samples its copy-on-write surface instead of allocating a second full buffer.
- The vector renderer resolves pattern paints from the document's pattern table and samples them in the document's colour mode, for the fill and the stroke independently (`Paint::Pattern`, `CompiledShape::with_patterns`, `render_shape_with_patterns`). The CPU and GPU fill/stroke split for clipped layers and interior effects uses the same patterns.
- `shape.create` and `shape.edit` accept and report the complete paint model. Malformed values return errors before the document changes. A pattern paint resolves a document or library pattern and embeds its tile in the same undo step.
- Copy/Paste Fill and Copy/Paste Stroke keep a snapshot of the referenced pattern. Pasting still works after the source document is closed, and pasting refuses to overwrite a different pattern that has the same id.

## Review fixes (2026-10-15)

- Pattern sampling accepts every finite positive `f32` scale, including `0.0001`, using a finite `f64` inverse.
- The shape split cache includes retained pattern tile memory in its conservative byte accounting. An entry larger than the budget stays uncached without evicting existing entries.
- Regression tests cover the small-scale sampler and cache accounting/oversize behavior.

## Validation of the updated code

Validated at `e22a9baedceefd97daffe84403b23c99c56d6919`:

- Windows: format, bundled translation catalogs, full workspace tests with HEIF, Clippy with warnings denied, dependency layering and scorecard checks passed.
- Ubuntu: the same checks, the no-HEIF tests, full workspace tests with the CI-pinned Craft fonts, all 24 WASM checks, real-file corpus tests and mdBook passed.
- The Web build passed in a targeted retry after restoring three local checkout files to their exact committed LF bytes. The initial packaging invocation had stopped on CRLF before building; no Git content change was needed. Source snapshots stayed unchanged during all validation runs.
- The production Web WASM is 25,041,756 bytes against this branch's 25,165,824-byte limit, leaving 124,068 bytes. The limit and features were not changed.
- Focused regressions reproduced the pattern-scale and cache-budget failures before the fix and passed afterward. The corrected code also received an independent local review.

A paired release comparison against the previous PR head used a 6000×4000 rectangle with pattern fill and a 12 px stroke. Across three paired processes per revision, cold median render times changed from 295.5 to 307.9 ms for a 128×128 tile and from 343.8 to 353.8 ms for a 2048×2048 tile; the measured ranges overlapped. Warm cache-hit medians were 35–43 µs, and output pixel hashes matched. The cache byte count is conservative retained-memory accounting, not a measured RAM total. These two CPU cases do not establish a general performance guarantee.

Refs #2496, #3446

I read all 14 changed-file patches and checked the transaction path. The small-scale correction is present: every finite positive f32 scale uses a finite f64 inverse, rather than silently reverting below the old threshold. prs.title: Layer Style: Gradient Overlay takes any number of colour stops (#5177)
prs.body:
Closes #5177.

The Gradient Overlay page modelled its gradient as a From and To colour, so a rainbow gradient on text, as in Photoshop, was impossible. Richer gradients (from PSDs or styles) only survived the dialog through its snapshot.

## Engine

- `layer.layerStyle.gradientOverlay` (and a gradient `stroke`) take `"stops": [[position, "#rrggbb" | [r, g, b]], …]` (2 to 256, sorted) and `"opacityStops": [[position, opacity %], …]` (`[]` is opaque), replacing From/To. The parameter docs say so.
- Malformed lists are refused at the command entry (`set` and `replace`) as bad params, so a bad edit changes nothing. Given lists replace the gradient's; without them, intermediate stops still survive an edit as before.

## Dialog

- The page shows a ramp with colour-stop markers, edited like the Gradient Editor: click under the ramp to add a stop with the gradient's colour there, drag a marker to move it, drag it away to delete it (two always stay), double-click it or the Color swatch to open the shared Color Picker on that stop. Location and Delete act on the selected stop, and a dropdown offers the Gradients panel's presets to start from.
- The page always writes `stops` and `opacityStops`, in the command's own grammar; the factory From/To defaults become two stops. Transparency stops are carried through, not edited on the page.
- The Color Picker request grows an optional `stop` index, also on the control channel (`ui.dialog.open {kind: "colorPicker", parent, effect, field: "stops", stop: i}`), documented in docs/control-protocol.md.

## Tests
