prs.title: Play CopyCat, AJ and Line and Color action sets; keep patterns across restarts; Shift Edge scale
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR makes three more real Photoshop action sets work in PhotoCraft, keeps imported patterns across restarts, and fixes a Select and Mask scale that drew a thick black band around Debaser's distressed ink. It follows #4698, which made the TrueGrit Texture Supply sets play. Every change comes from playing a real, published action set and fixing what stopped it, not from guessing at what Photoshop users might need.

## Why it started

This comes from testing PhotoCraft against the third-party and custom actions I use in my own workflow. The testing is ongoing: each set that doesn't play yet becomes the next fix. Running that collection in a build of #4698 showed three problems:

- Debaser's Ink Distressing actions drew a heavy black outline around all the line art, and small details merged into solid black.
- The tutorial folder held three action sets the importer had never seen: COPYCAT, AJ\_Actions2023 and LineAndColorTutorial.
- Every action that uses a pattern needed the `.pat` file reloaded in each new session.

| Set | Steps | Unmapped before | Unmapped after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COPYCAT | 244 | 44 | 0 |
| AJ\_Actions2023 | 35 | 8 | 4 |
| LineAndColorTutorial | 34 | 3 | 0 |

## Shift Edge: the black outline

Shift Edge at ±100% now moves an edge by its own softness, with a 1 px minimum, instead of a fixed 4 px. That turns Debaser's 8 px black band into a thin rim.

**Cause.** Debaser copies the ink shape onto a distress-texture layer as its mask, then shrinks that mask twice with Select and Mask Shift Edge −100%. Wherever the texture's mask doesn't reach, the ink stays solid black. PhotoCraft treated −100% as "move the edge `max(radius, 4)` px", so with Radius 0 the two passes left 8 px untextured around every edge. The 4 px figure came in with a work-in-progress commit and was never measured against Photoshop.

**Options considered.**

| Option | Why not, or why |
| --- | --- |
| Scale to edge softness (chosen) | Adobe describes Shift Edge as moving soft-edged borders. A hard mask has little border to move, so about 1 px per pass matches the intent of an action that runs it twice |
| Fix only `.atn` playback | Leaves the guessed 4 px in the Select and Mask dialog, so the same action recorded in PhotoCraft would still be wrong |
| Wait for a Photoshop reference | No Photoshop on the test machine. The fix can be refined to an exact scale once a reference render exists |

**The rule.** 100% equals `max(radius, feather, 2 × smooth σ)`, at least 1 px. A side-by-side render of line art with gaps from 2 px to 17 px confirmed it: the old build closed every gap in black, and the new one keeps even the 2 px gap open.

**Caveat.** This affects Select and Mask everywhere, not just actions, and its exact scale is still unverified against Photoshop.

## Action mappings

Almost every unmapped step already had a PhotoCraft command, so the importer just learned to recognise how Photoshop records it. New engine behaviour was added only where playing a real set proved it was needed.

**Mapped onto existing commands:** Create Clipping Mask, Apply Locking and lock settings, Blending Options' Advanced checkboxes, Diffuse, Delete Layer Mask, smart filter Blending Options, Shift-click layer ranges, and Select and Mask's newer "output to selection". Each one exports back to `.atn` too, and a round-trip test covers it.

**Engine changes, each forced by a step that failed:**

| Change | Why |
| --- | --- |
| New `history.clear` | Photoshop's Clear History clears only the current document. The nearest existing command, Purge › Histories, clears every open document, which is wrong for an action |
| `history.newSnapshot` takes `replaceExisting` | CopyCat retakes its "before/after sharpness" snapshots each run |
| `deleteFilterMask` takes `ifPresent` | Photoshop adds an empty filter mask with the first smart filter, and CopyCat deletes it. PhotoCraft never adds one, so the delete must quietly do nothing. This copies the `ifPresent` approach #4698 used for Layer From Background |
| Bring to Front / Send to Back on a layer already there returns `{"moved": false}` | CopyCat brings a new layer to the front of its group when it's already there. Photoshop doesn't stop, so PhotoCraft shouldn't. No undo step is added |
| Save in an Edit Contents document saves into the smart object | CopyCat edits a smart object's contents and then saves. The desktop app already did this from the menu, but playback looked for a file path and failed |

**Fixed while testing:** a Shift-click range of layers was replayed as a plain click, so CopyCat grouped one layer instead of two. It now replays as a range.

**Left unmapped on purpose:**

- AJ's Lens Correction carries a recorded camera lens profile. Mapping it to something that doesn't correct the same way would be a silent wrong result, so playback stops there with a clear message.
- Timeline frame steps and an empty Set have no effect on the document in PhotoCraft. They import switched off rather than counting as failures.

## Persistent patterns

Imported and defined patterns are now saved in the app's preset store and come back on the next launch, as Photoshop keeps its Patterns panel. Brushes, gradients and actions already persisted; patterns were the gap.

**Storage.** The store gets a small `patterns.json` index (order, names, full sizes) plus one `.pat` file per pattern, saved next to `actions.json`.

- One file per pattern, rather than one big `.pat`, means a pattern is written once. A rename rewrites only the index, and a delete removes only that pattern's files.
- The `.pat` format already had a tested reader and writer, and the files open in Photoshop too.
- Built-in patterns are never written; they're regenerated at startup.

**Why large patterns load on use.** Debaser's colour libraries are six `.pat` files of about 1.2 GB each, every pattern a 4500 × 4500 px texture. Loading saved patterns whole at startup would take about 7 GB of memory on every launch. Instead:

- Patterns over 128 px are saved with a small preview file, and only the preview loads at startup.
- The full pixels are read from disk the first time something paints with the pattern: a fill, a Pattern Fill layer, Pattern Stamp, a layer style, a brush texture or an export.
- All of those already go through one lookup function, so loading on demand needed changes in one place, not in each feature. This follows how saved brush tips already load.

**Safety rules.** A corrupt pattern file or index is skipped with a warning and never overwritten or deleted, so a later fix can still recover it. If a pattern can't be saved, you get one warning, not one after every action.

**Panel folders.** The Patterns panel removes folder entries whose pattern is missing. Because the store loads in the background, that would have emptied saved folders at every launch. The panel now waits until the store has loaded.

## Verification and open questions

All checks pass on top of current `main`. The real action files were played end to end as well.

- **Tests:** engine 1,594, UI 2,667, the Shift Edge tests, clippy with warnings as errors, the `panic_hunt` fuzz test, layering and the engine wasm check. New tests cover every new mapping (round trip), Save in Edit Contents, `ifPresent`, Bring to Front at the front, Clear History, replace-existing snapshots, and patterns surviving a restart: rename, delete, corrupt files and large patterns loading on use.
- **Real files:** all three CopyCat actions ran end to end with `COPYCAT PATTERNS.pat`, producing the expected photocopy look. AJ and Line and Color played up to the stops described above.
- **Problems already on `main`, not from this PR:** `cargo fmt --check` flags two UI files, and the UI crate's wasm check fails on `tile_overlay.rs`.

**Still open:**

- [x] Measure Shift Edge −100% against a Photoshop render, to replace "about 1 px" with Photoshop's real scale
- [x] Re-run Debaser Ink Distressing with its real texture `.pat` (so far tested with a stand-in noise pattern)
- [x] Decide whether to map Lens Correction once PhotoCraft can apply a recorded lens profile
- [x] Keep running the rest of the collection and send what still fails as the next PR

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

That is a visible change for anyone with saved Select and Mask settings or actions that used large values, and the PR description explains why. The tests are updated to match.

prs.title: Actions: add editable PhotoCraft Essentials starter presets
prs.body:
The Actions panel currently starts empty, so trying a basic action requires recording or importing one first. This adds an editable **PhotoCraft Essentials** set: **Auto Tone, Auto Contrast, Auto Color, Select Subject, and Blur Background**.

Closes #4779.

- Seed the set once after saved actions load on desktop/web, preserving existing names, order, edits, and unreadable action-store files. A persisted marker respects later deletion or renaming.
- Add **Load Default Actions** to the Actions flyout and empty panel, backed by `actions.loadDefaults` for CLI/MCP. Restoring adds missing names without overwriting custom actions. Headless sessions stay empty until explicitly loaded; recording/playback cannot mutate the library through this command.
- Use original editable command recipes, with no Photoshop action assets. Select Subject samples visible layers. The auto adjustments retain their existing behavior.
- Add atomic `layer.blurBackground` for the fifth preset (default radius 8). It detects the subject on the active pixel layer, excludes subject coverage from Gaussian color sampling, and blends the result inside the current selection. It preserves transparency, selection, masks, other layers and off-canvas pixels, with one Undo. No detected subject or cancellation commits no edit. This avoids a recorded Subject → Inverse → Blur sequence accidentally using an old selection after detection fails.

Blur Background uses PhotoCraft's existing heuristic subject detector and Gaussian Blur. Detection quality remains that algorithm's limitation; partially covered edge pixels can still contribute to sampling. This is not depth-aware lens blur or a claim of semantic segmentation parity. The existing Actions player runs steps synchronously; the underlying command supports background-job cancellation when invoked directly through the UI dispatcher.

Validation at final head `61d9e8cc1aed29ed6bea0d0fd2702fa87c4f0206`:

- [CI run 38754105890](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38754105890) passed: Windows and Ubuntu tests, strict Clippy, dependency layering, corpus tests, wasm32 checks, and the browser build/size gate. Ubuntu also passed the test variants without HEIF and with craft-fonts. [Documentation](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38754106014) passed. The fuzz job was intentionally skipped by the workflow.
- The denied-storage regression was reproduced before the fix; all 16 browser persistence tests passed locally afterward. The original assertion remains intact. Defaults and their seed marker can still be staged for persistence, while unsaved-change warnings track user changes separately, including failure/retry and changes made during an in-flight write.
- Merged current main `4e7a17cd`; all visible checks above cover the resulting final head.

Feature-specific validation before the latest main merge:

- Engine/UI tests: **4,570 passed**, 32 opt-in tests ignored. Blur tests cover actual preset playback and one-step Undo/Redo at 8/16/32-bit, selection/alpha/mask/off-canvas preservation, invalid targets/locks/parameters, cancellation and no-subject failure. Sampling tests cover RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab and both Gaussian implementations.
- Offscreen UI: selected **Blur Background** by clicking its row and the actual **Play selection** footer button. Inspected before/after screenshots of an original synthetic fixture using the CPU canvas (`--safe-gpu`). Background texture is smoothed while subject texture remains sharp.
- Layering, wasm, parity, and the separately run ignored `panic_hunt` test passed. Generated parity output was unchanged.
- Release timing on a 6000 × 4000 synthetic image: **1.5904 seconds** for the whole Blur Background command at radius 8, including detection, on an Apple M1 Pro. Release build used LTO off and 16 codegen units. This is a new operation with no safe equivalent command to use as a before-change baseline.

approval.body:
Read the whole change outside the docs and translations. CI is green at 61d9e8c (Linux and Windows tests, corpus, wasm and the size gate).

- **Seeding:** the starter set is seeded once, tracked by `defaults_version` in `actions.json`, so a later delete or rename stays. Existing names and edits win, in-memory and on-disk actions are never overwritten, and an unreadable or unsupported `actions.json` is neither seeded nor written. The tests cover those cases and the explicit "Load Default Actions" restore. The command is unavailable during recording or playback.
- **Web bridge:** generated defaults count as unsaved work only once the user edits them, so a failed first write doesn't raise a loss-of-work warning, and a newer edit during a transaction still gets its own write. The four new bridge tests pin this.
- **`layer.blurBackground`:** one atomic job. It checks the target (raster only, pixel and all locks, including a locked parent) and the radius, and a cancellation or "no subject found" commits nothing. The background colours are blurred with subject coverage excluded from the alpha, so foreground colour doesn't bleed. The result is blended only within the current selection, leaving alpha, masks, other layers and off-canvas pixels as they were. The tests cover this at 8, 16 and 32 bits and in every colour mode.

The description is clear that the subject detector is the existing heuristic and not depth-aware blur, which sets expectations correctly.

prs.title: fix(mixer-brush): Alt-click samples the foreground colour like the Brush (#4873)
prs.body:
Fixes #4873.

Holding Alt with the Mixer Brush did nothing: `alt_samples` in `canvas.rs`, which decides which painting tools turn into the Eyedropper while Alt is held, listed the Brush, Pencil, Gradient and Paint Bucket but not the Mixer Brush. This adds `Tool::MixerBrush` to that list, so Alt-click (and held or latched Alt, which go through the same check) samples the foreground colour and shows the Eyedropper cursor, as with the Brush. Control+Alt stays the brush-resize drag.

Tests:
- `alt_click_with_the_mixer_brush_samples_the_foreground` (alt_click_tests.rs): Alt-click on a red pixel with the Mixer Brush sets the foreground to red and paints nothing.
- An extra assertion in the `alt_samples` unit test.

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Approving `23bab3cc9204568aaeb012b9e1da70a2caacb879`. This replaces my earlier approval of `5244ee7c`, which made Alt-click set the foreground.

I re-read the whole diff against @tanish2k09's notes. Both points are addressed:
- **Alt-click loads the reservoir and leaves the foreground alone.** `MixerBrush` is out of `alt_samples`. Alt-click and Alt-drag now go through the new `paint.mixerLoad` (`brush_cmds.rs:691`), which samples with `sample_cmds::sample_color` and follows the Mixer Brush's Sample All Layers option (overridable with `sampleAllLayers`) and the Eyedropper's Sample Size (`canvas.rs:5128`). Over transparency or off the canvas, nothing is loaded. This matches Adobe's description: Alt-click loads paint from the canvas into the reservoir, and choosing a foreground colour loads that colour instead.
- **The Eyedropper cursor stays while Alt is held.** `alt_picks` feeds the cursor, `alt_eyedropper` and `alt_grab::alt_click_tool`. Control+Alt is still the brush-resize drag.
- The sample now survives the next stroke: `mixer_brush` keeps it while the foreground is unchanged and no `color` is passed (`brush_cmds.rs:653`, `MixerState::holds_sample` in `mixer.rs:66`). The UI's Mixer Brush stroke passes no `color` (`retouch_ui.rs:95`), so the load really is what gets painted. With Load after Stroke on, the reservoir is refilled with the sample, as in Photoshop.
- CodeRabbit's point is handled too: the invalid-input case now checks that the reservoir, the foreground and the revision don't change.

**What I ran:** I used a fresh worktree on this head, merged with current main (it merges cleanly). `cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check` is clean, and `clippy -p photocraft-paint -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. The lib tests pass: engine 1738, paint 106 and ui-egui 3035, plus `panic_hunt`'s default test. I also reverted parts of the fix: removing the `holds_sample` branch fails `mixer_load_fills_the_reservoir_from_the_canvas_and_keeps_the_foreground`, and removing the Mixer Brush arm in `alt_eyedropper` fails `alt_click_with_the_mixer_brush_loads_the_reservoir_not_the_foreground`. Hosted CI is green on this head, including both Windows jobs. I tested on Linux only and didn't try it interactively.

**Non-blocking**
- Please update the PR title and description. They still say "Alt-click samples the foreground colour like the Brush", which is the opposite of what the PR does now and would end up in the squash commit.
- Because `holds_sample` compares the reservoir with the foreground captured at sampling time, changing the foreground and then changing it back (for example pressing X twice) brings the old canvas sample back instead of the foreground. That's a small oddity. Clearing `sampled_over` whenever the foreground is set would avoid it, but it doesn't need to block this PR.
- Photoshop loads a multi-coloured patch unless Load Solid Colors Only is on, so this PR covers the solid-colour case only, as you said. A follow-up issue for Load Solid Colors Only and patterned loads would keep track of that gap.

prs.title: Layer Style: Photoshop's layout (three columns, OK/Cancel/New Style/Preview on the right, one-line rows) [depends on #4938]
prs.body:
**Depends on #4938** (one dialog size on every page; it reuses that PR's fixed-size `Sizing`). This branch includes its commit; review the second commit, `feat(layer-style): Photoshop's layout`, or merge #4938 first.

## Screenshots

Blending Options, side by side.

**Photoshop 2026**

![Photoshop 2026 Layer Style dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OctaNebula/photocraft/pr-images/5010-photoshop.png)

**This PR**

![PhotoCraft Layer Style dialog with this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OctaNebula/photocraft/pr-images/5010-this-pr.png)

**Before** (the old layout; this capture comes from a build with #4938's earlier resize grip, widened. On `main` the dialog is 600 pt wide and its height changes per page.)

![PhotoCraft Layer Style dialog before this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OctaNebula/photocraft/pr-images/5010-before.png)

## Problem

Our Layer Style is tall and narrow: OK / Cancel sit in a row at the bottom, Preview and New Style… are on the pages, and every slider sits under its label on a line of its own. Photoshop's (2026) is wide and short, about 777 × 525: three columns, with OK, Cancel, New Style…, Preview and a live preview swatch on the right, and each slider on one line with its label and field.

## What changes

- **Three columns** (`layer_style::body`): the effect list, the selected page, and a right-hand column with **OK**, **Cancel**, **New Style…**, **Preview** and a **preview swatch**. The list and the page are framed and scroll on their own. The dialog draws its own OK / Cancel and takes Enter, like Guide Layout (`dialogs.rs` skips its shared button row for Layer Style).
- **Photoshop's size**: 800 × 550 (Photoshop: ~777 × 525; our rows are a little taller), at most the window. Every page fits without scrolling at that size, Blending Options and Bevel & Emboss included.
- **One-line rows**: `widgets::slider_line` puts the label (right-aligned in a column, `widgets::row_label`), the slider and the value field on one line; the label still scrubs the field. Dropdowns, colours, the angle dial (`widgets::angle_dial_line`) and contours use the same label column, and check boxes sit under the controls, as in Photoshop. The Blending Options page uses them too.
- **Preview swatch**: the dialog's pending style on Photoshop's sample square (`presets::styles::thumbnail`), built on a scratch layer the way the canvas preview builds it on the real one, cached until the style changes. While the mouse is down (a slider drag) it renders at point size, ~6 ms a change in a dev build, and re-renders at screen resolution when released.
- **List bar** under the effect list, as in Photoshop: **fx** (the Layers panel's button and press-menu) adds an effect, or turns on and shows the layer's one for a kind that takes one; **▲ / ▼** move the selected instance among those of its kind; the **bin** deletes it.
- **+** on every kind that takes several instances, also when the layer has none yet.
- Three new tooltips ("Move effect up", "Move effect down", "Delete effect") are translated in the 20 complete catalogs.
- **Current Layer**: Blend If's first bar is labelled "Current Layer:" as in Photoshop 2026 (it was "This Layer:"; the `thisLayer` field is unchanged). It and "Underlying Layer:" are now translated in all 20 complete catalogs (the latter was missing from 15).

The engine is untouched: the dialog's fields, OK (`layer.layerStyle.replace` …) and automation (`ui.dialog.set` / `ui.dialog.confirm`) work as before.

## Tests

- `layer_style_is_laid_out_like_photoshops`: wider than tall; the list left of the page; OK, Cancel, New Style…, Preview right of it, top to bottom.
- `layer_style_ok_cancel_and_enter`: OK applies the style, Cancel drops it, Enter is OK; each closes the dialog.
- `layer_style_bin_deletes_the_selected_effect`.
- `move_instance_reorders_within_its_kind` (also out-of-range moves and unknown ids), `fx_menu_adds_or_shows_an_effect`, `pending_style_is_the_dialogs_and_leaves_the_document_alone`.
- The existing Layer Style, dialog and #4938 tests pass unchanged apart from `body`'s new signature in five call sites.

Ran: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. I checked Bevel & Emboss, Blending Options, Drop Shadow, Stroke and Styles at 1440 × 900 and Bevel & Emboss at 1366 × 700 with the offscreen `snapshot` example.

## Not in this PR

- Photoshop's **Name** field at the top, and the **Contour** / **Texture** sub-rows under Bevel & Emboss (Texture needs engine support).
- The effect list's rows are painted, so screen readers and kittest can't name them (as before this PR).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: Prevent control-channel engine commands from editing behind modal dialogs
prs.body:
Fixes #4919.

The control channel applied the existing modal-dialog guard to `ui.menu.invoke` but bypassed it for `engine.execute`. Consequently, automation could change a document while an adjustment dialog still displayed its original state.

Apply the same modal-availability policy to both command entry points.

Keep the existing Camera Raw continuation exception, which operates on its active dialog rather than issuing an unrelated document command.

Added a regression test that:
- Opens a Hue/Saturation dialog.
- Rejects Invert through both command entry points.
- Confirms the document revision and dialog fields remain unchanged.
- Verifies the command succeeds after the dialog is cancelled.

Tests added but not executed locally.

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Approving `81964dc5ef77a71a2ae2a938958cf3ed77d90719`.

I read the whole diff. The control channel's `engine.execute` skipped the modal gate that `ui.menu.invoke` has, so a client could edit the document behind an open dialog. The `modal_allows` check now applies to both methods, with the existing Camera Raw continuation exception, and the error text changes to "command is unavailable while a modal dialog is open". The test opens the Hue/Saturation dialog, shows both methods are refused with the revision and the dialog's fields unchanged, and then shows `engine.execute` works after Cancel. Hosted CI is green.

I did not run the tests locally. Worth knowing: the removed comment said `engine.execute` was "deliberately not subject" to this gate, so this reverses an earlier design choice; any automation client that executes engine commands while a dialog is open will now get an error. prs.title: Preserve Dissolve coverage when compositing clipped layers
prs.body:
Fixes #4921.

Clipped layers using Dissolve were composited through the ordinary blend path, producing fractional transparency instead of Dissolve's binary pixel coverage.

Apply the deterministic Dissolve coverage decision before compositing clipped layers in both the CPU renderer and GPU shader.

The correction:
- Uses the source alpha, layer opacity and fill opacity.
- Produces the expected stochastic source-or-backdrop pixels.
- Preserves the clipping base's alpha.
- Uses document-coordinate noise to keep the pattern stable across rendering regions.

Added a CPU regression test for binary coverage, opacity/fill interaction and clipping boundaries, plus GPU parity cases at different opacity and fill settings.

Tests added but not executed locally.

approval.body:
Approving `194a8976cd6c14441222b287b9b4f4841a0eb2f9`.

I read the whole diff. A clipped Dissolve layer was composited with the ordinary partial-alpha blend, which lost Dissolve's binary coverage (#4921). Now both the CPU path (`composite_atop_any`) and the GPU path (`fs_atop`) decide coverage per pixel by comparing `dissolve_noise` at document coordinates with source alpha times opacity (times fill on the CPU), then composite as Normal at full strength and keep the base's alpha. The tests are good: the output contains only exact source or base pixels, with the coverage near 0.6 x 0.5, the clip hidden outside the base, whole-render versus partial-region equality at 8, 16 and 32 bit with a negative origin, and a CPU/GPU parity case at two opacity/fill pairs. prs.title: Layer Style: one dialog size on every page, and it fits short screens
prs.body:
## Problem

The Layer Style dialog's height jumps with each page: it is sized by its content, so Drop Shadow, Blending Options and Bevel & Emboss each make it a different height (Photoshop's keeps one size). Bevel & Emboss makes it about 732 pt tall, and nothing scrolls, so on a window shorter than that (a 768 pt laptop screen once the taskbar and title bar are taken) OK and Cancel are pushed off the bottom.

## Fix

- **One size** (`dialogs.rs`): Layer Style is drawn in a fixed-size `egui::Resize` area, the same path the web-page dialog already uses (now a small `Sizing` per dialog: size, minimum, resizable or not, outline). It is 600 × 760, the room the tallest page needs on a 900 pt screen, and no larger than the window less a margin. It is **not** resizable, as in Photoshop; the web-page dialog keeps its resize grip.
- **Fits and scrolls** (`layer_style.rs`): the effects list and the settings page each sit in a vertical scroll area as tall as the dialog leaves them, so a short window scrolls the page and OK / Cancel stay visible. The separator follows that height (it was a fixed 330 pt), and the settings column takes the dialog's width. The Styles gallery lost its own fixed 340 pt scroll area: the page scrolls now. The Blend If bars were capped at 320 pt; they span the column, so they stay under their 0 / 255 labels.
- **Title band** (`dialogs.rs`): a `Resize` clips its contents to its area, which cut off the strip around the title that #1945 made draggable (#1921). This already broke that strip on the web-page dialog on `main`. The sized area's clip now reaches the 7 pt the title band extends (`TITLE_REACH`); the existing `layer_style_title_gutters_can_start_drags` test covers it.

Hide whitespace when reviewing `layer_style.rs` (`?w=1`): most of its diff is re-indentation from the two scroll areas.

## Tests

- `layer_style_keeps_one_size_on_every_page`: Bevel & Emboss, Blending Options and Styles show at the same size, with no resize grip.
- `layer_style_fits_a_short_screen`: on a 1366 × 640 window, Bevel & Emboss fits on screen with OK and Cancel visible.
- `dragging_the_title_bar_moves_the_dialog` now runs on a 1100 pt-tall window: at its fixed height the dialog left only 63 pt of room below it for the test's 80 pt drag, and the on-screen clamp stopped it there.

Ran: `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`. I checked the dialog at 1440 × 900 and 1366 × 700 with the offscreen `snapshot` example.

## Not in this PR

Photoshop's Layer Style is wide and short (about 777 × 525): OK, Cancel, New Style…, Preview and a preview swatch sit in a column on the right, and each slider shares a line with its label and field. Ours stacks each slider under its label and puts OK / Cancel at the bottom, so it is tall and narrow. That layout is #5010, which builds on this PR and makes this fixed size Photoshop's.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: Filter > Other > Frequency Separation (#1714)
prs.body:
Closes #1714.

**Filter › Other › Frequency Separation…** sets up frequency separation in one step, instead of the duplicate / Gaussian Blur / Apply Image / blend mode routine.

From the active pixel layer it adds a **Frequency Separation** group right above it, holding:

- **Low Frequency** (Normal): the layer through Gaussian Blur at the chosen radius. These are the same pixels Filter › Blur › Gaussian Blur produces.
- **High Frequency** (Linear Light): `High = (Source − Low) / 2 + ½` in each colour channel, keeping the source's transparency.

This is Photoshop's recipe: Apply Image › Subtract, Scale 2, Offset 128 in 8-bit, and Add + Invert, Scale 2, Offset 0 in 16-bit, which give the same values. Linear Light computes `Low + 2·High − 1`, so the result is the source again. In 32-bit our Linear Light uses the same formula, so the recipe is unchanged there. The source layer itself is not modified, it is one history step, and the High layer ends up targeted, ready for healing.

The command is `layer.frequencySeparation` with `{"radius": 0.1..1000 = 4}`. From the menu it opens the existing schema dialog, which has a single Radius field. Photoshop has no menu item for this (people record it as an action), so the id is our own. The menu entry goes after Color to Alpha (`PLACE_AFTER`). I kept it out of `filter.*` because it adds layers rather than filtering the target, so mask/channel routing, Fade and Last Filter would all be wrong for it. The menu label is in all 17 catalogs, which the coverage test requires.

**Limits**

- Only RGB and Grayscale. In CMYK and Lab the compositor does not blend on the stored values (in a test the rebuild was off by 0.7 and 0.14), so the command is refused there rather than giving a wrong split.
- Linear Light clips to 0..1, so 32-bit values above 1 come back as 1.
- 8-bit stores High to the nearest level, so the rebuild is within ±1 level, the same as Photoshop's recipe.
- The new layers carry only the source's pixels (no mask, style, opacity or blending options), and the selection is ignored. The rebuild is exact for an opaque, Normal, 100% layer, which is the normal case for this technique.
- It is refused, with a message, on non-pixel layers (type, shape, adjustment, group, smart object), on empty layers, and when a channel, Quick Mask or layer mask is targeted.

Validation:
- Engine tests in the module: the composite of Low + High with the source hidden matches the source at 8/16/32-bit RGB and 8/32-bit Gray (tolerance 1/255, 1/65535, 1e-5); Low equals Gaussian Blur at radii 2 and 6.5; group/layer names, order, blend modes and the targeted layer; High's bounds equal the source's; one undo restores the document exactly and redo brings the result back; works on the Background; refusals listed above; bad params give `BadParams` and leave the document unchanged.
- Each new test was checked against a mutation that should break it: High without `/2`, mask/mask-view/colour-mode checks removed, Linear Light left out, radius ignored, empty-layer check removed. All of them failed.
- `cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` passes.
- ui-egui: `menus::`, `filter_dialog::` and `i18n::` tests pass, including a new one for the menu position and dialog.
- `cargo clippy -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` all pass. `cargo xtask parity` leaves the checklist unchanged.
- Checked rendered with the offscreen `snapshot` example: the Layers panel after the command, and the Radius dialog. (macOS, Apple silicon)
- Full `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui`: `new_doc_ui::tests::new_document_depth_labels_and_tooltips_are_translated` and `prefs_ui::tests::preference_labels_are_translated` fail the same way on `main`

Read the whole source diff apart from the translation files. Filter > Other > Frequency Separation adds a group above the active pixel layer with a Gaussian-blurred "Low Frequency" layer and a "High Frequency" layer set to Linear Light, as one history step.

- The maths is right: High is (source - Low) / 2 + 0.5 in the colour channels, computed from the stored Low (quantised at 8 and 16 bits), so Low plus High on Linear Light rebuilds the source. The test checks that through the compositor with the source hidden, at 8, 16 and 32 bits in RGB and grey, within one level. A second test breaks the blend mode to prove the first one is not passing by accident.
- Transparency is handled: High stays transparent where the source is, so its bounds match the source and mid-grey does not fill whole tiles, and layers without alpha are computed over the canvas. Work is done in bounded batches of tiles, so a large layer does not allocate the whole f32 copy.
- Eligibility is strict: only an RGB or grey document, only a pixel layer with pixels, and never a targeted mask, channel or Quick Mask. Refusals leave the document untouched, and the tests cover type, adjustment, group, smart object, empty layer and channel cases.
- Low is checked to equal what Gaussian Blur makes of the same layer at the same radius, and one undo removes the whole group.

prs.title: fix(cmyk): Flatten Image and merges keep the inks of a tagged CMYK document (#3778)
prs.body:
Fixes #3778

## What was wrong

PhotoCraft composites in RGB. For a CMYK document, the layers are read through the document's embedded CMYK profile (for example U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2), but the composite was separated back to CMYK through the built-in coated profile. So the pixels were read with one profile and written with another. Every pixel of a tagged CMYK document moved on Layer › Flatten Image, even with only a Background layer. The same flatten path also serves Stamp Visible, Merge Visible, Merge Layers, Copy Merged, Background from Layer and Rasterize Layer Style. Merge Down also built its temporary document without the document's profile.

## What changed

- `compose::flatten_to_surface`, the engine's `composite_layers` and Rasterize Layer Style now separate the composite through the document's own CMYK profile. Merge Down's temporary document keeps the profile.
- When a CMYK document's composite is a single plain pixel layer (Normal, 100 % opacity and fill, no masks, effects, Blend If, channel exclusion or advanced blending, same depth), Flatten copies its inks exactly, as Photoshop does. Black isn't regenerated, and inks outside the display gamut aren't clipped. Partly transparent pixels that are flattened onto paper still go through the compositor.
- `photocraft_io::merged_composite`, the helper that turns a PSD's stored merged image into RGB for corpus comparisons, now reads CMYK through the file's embedded profile. Before, every comparison of a CMYK file tagged with a non-default profile was off.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/cmyk_flatten_profile.rs`: a CMYK document at 8 and 16 bit, tagged and untagged, holding separations plus inks no separation produces (K only, rich black, solid cyan, paper). After Flatten Image, Stamp Visible and Background from Layer the inks are bit-identical. After Merge Down and Merge Visible (which go through RGB) they stay within the profile's own round trip. prs.title: fix(layer-style): support Blend If Alt-split handle feathering and throttle live preview
prs.body:
### Summary
1. Fixes Blend If slider handle interaction: Alt-dragging a black or white triangle now splits it into two half-handles (`[min, max]`) for smooth feathered luminance blending, matching Photoshop 1:1.
2. Resolves heavy CPU spikes and stuttering during slider drag by throttling live Layer Style document preview compositing to ~30 FPS on the UI thread.

### Details
- **Alt-Split Triangle Handles:** Refactored slider drag math in `blend_if_bar` (`layer_style.rs`). Alt-dragging the black triangle splits the right half (`[0, max]`); Alt-dragging the white triangle splits the left half (`[min, 255]`). Dragging halves back together seamlessly reunites them. Handle ordering `0 <= black_lo <= black_hi <= white_lo <= white_hi <= 255` is strictly maintained.
- **Live Preview CPU Throttling:** In `canvas.rs`, dragging sliders previously triggered full synchronous CPU composite passes on every pointer move event (up to 120+ times/sec), pegging CPU cores at 100%. Live Layer Style preview rendering is now throttled to ~30 FPS (>= 33ms) during rapid drag gestures, while guaranteeing the final state is always rendered immediately upon release or timer trigger.
- Adds `[people.Gotix-eg]` to `contributors/people.toml`.

### Testing
- Added unit test `blend_if_alt_split_and_drag_behavior` verifying Alt-split, dragging split halves, seamless reunion, drag without Alt, and boundary clamping.
- All 30 unit tests in `layer_style` pass (`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib layer_style::tests`).
- Zero clippy warnings (`cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib -- -D warnings`).
- Layering verified (`cargo xtask layers`).

approval.body:
Read the whole diff and the surrounding `blend_if_bar` / `blend_quad` code. The drag is now a small state machine (`BlendDrag`: Pair, Split, Single) kept across frames, so Alt-dragging an unsplit Blend If handle splits it toward the pointer and dragging a half back over the other reunites it, as in Photoshop.

- `step_blend_drag` only calls `u8::clamp` with ordered bounds: `blend_quad` already forces `q[0] <= q[1] <= q[2] <= q[3]`, and no branch moves a value that a later clamp uses as a bound, so there is no `min > max` panic. The final pass keeps the quad ordered.
- Pair without Alt moves both halves together, bounded by the neighbouring pair; Single (an already split half) moves only that half between its neighbours.
- Hit-testing offsets by 2.5 px for split halves to match the half-triangles that are drawn, and the old `usize` drag key is replaced by the new type, so nothing else reads it.
- The new test walks a split, a move, the reunite, the white-side split, a solid drag and the clamp.

No defect found. All checks on this head pass.

prs.title: control: suggest near matches for unknown command ids and methods (#3674)
prs.body:
`engine.execute {"command": "engine.commands"}` failed with a bare ``unknown command `engine.commands` ``, so an agent that guessed an id had to list the whole registry to correct itself. Unknown protocol methods had the same problem.

`EngineError::UnknownCommand` now appends up to three registered ids close to the bad one, so every path that reports it (headless serve, the desktop control server, MCP `command_run`, `Session::disabled_reason`) gets the hint:

```
unknown command `engine.commands`; did you mean `command.list`?
unknown command `document.undo`; did you mean `edit.undo`, `history.undo` or `edit.purge.undo`?
unknown command `filter.blur.gaussian`; did you mean `filter.blur.gaussianBlur`?
```

Matching is deterministic and only runs on the error path: case-insensitive edit distance (the spell checker's existing Damerau-Levenshtein, now exposed as `photocraft_text::spell::edit_distance`), then ids that start with the given name, the same last segment in another namespace, and the same namespace with a longer last segment. `engine.commands` -> `command.list` is a small explicit table since spelling can't find it. No aliases are added (#3675 is left alone).

Both protocol servers also cover the reverse case. A protocol method sent through `engine.execute` (`doc.inspect`, `ui.inspect`) says it is a protocol method. An engine command id sent as a method (`edit.undo`) points at `engine.execute`. Other unknown methods get near method names. The desktop server gains a `METHODS` list for this, and a test checks that every entry is served.

Tests: new unit tests in `engine::command_hints`, `automation::rpc` and `ui-egui::control`, plus a case in `tests/mcp.rs`. The engine tests failed before the change. docs/control-protocol.md has a sentence on the new error text.

Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings and tests for text, engine, automation and ui-egui, plus `xtask layers` and `xtask wasm`. I didn't run the full workspace test locally and left that to CI. Three tests also fail on current main without this change: `workspace::tests::registry_filesystem_path_params_are_classified` (`edit.installedProfiles`), `adjust_params::tests::destructive_levels_dont_clip_in_32_bit` and `bridge_reports_unreachable_app` (a connect timeout on this WSL box). I haven't tried it by hand against a running desktop app.

Fixes #3674

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

approval.body: Read the whole diff. The hint is built only on the error path. `near_matches` ranks by spelling first (case or a few typos), then by prefix, the same last segment in another namespace, and the same namespace with a longer last segment, with ties broken by the closest spelling and then the name, so the output is deterministic and capped at three. `engine.commands` is aliased to `command.list`. A protocol method sent through `engine.execute`, and an engine command sent as a protocol method, each get a message that says which route to use. `disabled_reason_with` now returns the same text as the error, so every caller reports it the same way. `edit_distance` is a thin public wrapper over the existing Damerau-Levenshtein code. The tests cover the headless server, MCP `command_run`, the capped and ordered list, and the plain message when nothing is close. prs.title: feat(export): optionally trim transparent margins from layer files
prs.body:
## Problem

Layers to Files always exports each layer at the full document dimensions, even when its visible content occupies only a small area.

For workflows involving sprites, isolated assets, and reusable design elements, this leaves unnecessary transparent margins around every exported image.

Addresses #3447.

## Changes

- Add an optional `trim` parameter to `file.export.layersToFiles`.
- Expose a Trim checkbox in the Layers to Files dialog.
- Calculate the visible alpha bounds of each isolated layer before export.
- Crop the temporary export document to those bounds using the existing document-cropping implementation.
- Account for the rendered result, including masks and layer effects.
- Preserve full document dimensions when trimming is disabled.
- Keep entirely transparent layers exportable without creating zero-sized images.
- Leave the original document unchanged.

## Compatibility

Trimming is disabled by default, preserving existing export behavior and automation scripts.

The option applies independently to each exported layer.

## Tests

Added regression tests covering:
- Default full-canvas exports.
- Trimmed exports and pixel preservation.
- 8-, 16-, and 32-bit source documents.
- Non-destructive export behavior.
- Entirely transparent layers.

The tests have not been executed locally. CI validation is pending.

## Issue

Addresses #3447.

prs.title: fix(vector): target selected saved paths and own Pen gestures
prs.body:
Selecting a saved path in the Paths panel did not make the path tools target it: Path Selection, Free Transform Path, Direct Selection, Convert Point and Add/Delete Anchor Point kept editing the Work Path or the active shape. Unfinished Pen gestures could also survive a document switch and land in another tab.

Refs #2496, #1397. Builds on #4730 (#4721, a new Pen path joins the selected path) and #4526 (#4022, ⌘/Ctrl edits the path being drawn).

This PR was reduced to the path targeting and gesture ownership part. The Pen anchor editing, Convert glyph and cursor states that were in earlier revisions will follow in a separate PR on top of this one.

## Behavior

- **Selected saved paths are edited.** Path Selection, Free Transform Path, Direct Selection, Convert Point, Add/Delete Anchor Point and the Pen's Auto Add/Delete act on the work or saved path selected in the Paths panel. An explicit selection comes before the targeted vector mask or the active shape layer's path; without one, the existing fallbacks apply. The selected saved path is drawn on the canvas with the vector tools. Locked layers offer no edit.
- **Pen destination is captured at the first anchor.** Pen, Curvature Pen and Freeform Pen keep the target they started with (shape layer with its paint, selected path, vector mask or a new Work Path) until the single commit, even if the selection changes in between. The append behavior of #4730 is kept: after drawing, the path stays selected and the next path joins it.
- **Gestures belong to their document.** Pen drafts, Direct Selection anchors and drags, Path Selection drags and Freeform traces record document, revision and target. After a tab switch, a closed or reopened document, an external edit, or a tool/target change, the gesture is cancelled and its late pointer events are consumed. A Paths panel selection is never carried to a same-named path in another tab. Drafts and anchor selections restored from settings have no owner and are dropped.
- **Failed commits keep the draft.** If a Pen, Curvature Pen or Freeform commit is rejected, the exact draft stays, the error is shown, and it is not retried each frame. A ⌘/Ctrl press off the draft or a new Freeform trace cannot then edit another path.
- **`path.set` validates the result.** Appending a subpath (`op`) validates the complete path (finite, f32-representable coordinates, ≤ 4096 knots/subpaths, bounded tessellation) before an undoable edit is recorded.
- Direct Selection keeps its anchor selection across its own edits and arrow-key nudges (#4500), bound to the new revision.

No new commands, document fields or dependencies. Edits use the existing commands, one history step each.

## Validation

Rebased as one commit on current main (`99e11388`), merge-tree check against main is clean.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p photocraft-ui-egui -p photocraft-engine -p photocraft-vector --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`: pass.
- `photocraft-vector` and `photocraft-engine` tests pass, including the new `pen_path_append` test and `panic_hunt -- --ignored`.
- `photocraft-ui-egui --lib`: 2721 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored. New coverage: `pen_path_ownership_tests`, `pen_gesture_owner_tests`, saved-path cases in `direct_select_tests` / `anchor_tools_tests` (incl. arrow-key nudges on a saved path), Freeform ownership in `lasso_ui` and `vector_ui`.
- `photocraft-ui-egui --tests` (Windows): all 27 test binaries pass with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`. In a parallel run, `marquee_autoscroll` crashed with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` in the software GPU adapter (the same Windows WARP issue seen before on this machine); it passes serially. GitHub CI is the reference for the parallel run.

One upstream test expectation changed meaning with #4526: a ⌘/Ctrl press *on* the draft now edits it in place, so the failed-commit test presses off the draft instead.

## Screenshots

Synthetic offscreen capture (`pen_path_visual_tests`, run with `--ignored`): a saved path is selected in the Paths panel and dragged with Path Selection by the same offset.

| | Before drag | After drag |
|---|---|---|
| main (before this PR): the Work Path moves | ![Baseline before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Skyfuller1303/photocraft/edc0246bc0973a4dbb2f44383570796a6e387d33/baseline-before.png) | ![Baseline after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Skyfuller1303/photocraft/edc0246bc0973a4dbb2f44383570796a6e387d33/baseline-after.png) |
| This PR on current main: the selected saved curve moves, the Work Path stays | ![Selected saved path before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Skyfuller1303/photocraft/370930a634cd14ef236cb288b99c65def3aa2094/saved-path-before.png) | ![Selected saved path after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Skyfuller1303/photocraft/370930a634cd14ef236cb288b99c65def3aa2094/saved-path-after.png) |

The baseline row was captured earlier on main before #4730; Path Selection's targeting on main is unchanged since.

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. Pen, Freeform Pen, Path Selection, Direct Selection and the anchor tools now work on the work or saved path selected in the Paths panel, and their drags and drafts are tied to the document, revision and target they started on.

- The ownership checks compare the document id, the weak `Arc` pointer, the revision, the layer, the selected path, the vector-mask flag and the tool. So a reopened document with the same id and revision is still caught, and a stale drag is cancelled with its remaining pointer events swallowed.
- The Pen target is captured at the first anchor and committed once through `path.set` (with `combine` when appending), `layer.vectorMask.edit` or `shape.create`. A failed commit keeps the exact draft, marks it `commit_failed`, and is not retried each frame or on tool switch.
- `path.set` now validates the merged path before touching the document, so appending small components cannot get past the total knot and tessellation budget. The arithmetic guards in `validate_path` and `validate_workload` reject overflow, and the shape limits are unchanged.
- The runtime owner and drag are `serde(skip)`, so a draft or selection restored from settings is never applied to another tab.

The tests cover the cases above: reopen, revision, target and tool changes, failed commits, undo and redo, and the limits. CI is green at this head. The branch has a merge conflict and needs a rebase before it can merge.

prs.title: Replay recorded layer visibility on the intended named layer
prs.body:
Recorded layer-eye changes use document-local layer IDs, so replaying the action in another document can miss or affect the wrong layer.

Record visibility targets by layer name and duplicate-name ordinal, then resolve them consistently in engine and shell playback. Report missing targets and allow explicitly targeted visibility changes even when no layer is active. Existing recordings retain their behavior; newly recorded eye changes use the portable target.

Regression coverage: replay into another document, duplicate layer names, deselected layers, document Undo and shell playback.

Validation on current main (614d0689): engine and UI `actions` tests pass.

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. Recorded `layer.setProps` visibility gestures now store `_actionLayer {name, ordinal}` instead of a document-local layer id, and both the engine (`run_recorded`) and the shell (`actions::play`) resolve it through the shared `playback_params`, so replay hits the intended layer in another document and among duplicate names.

- A missing name or ordinal reports a failed step rather than touching another layer.
- The active layer is used when no `layer` was given, and `names_existing_layer` is widened only for visibility-only params.
- Both new tests cover the cross-document case, including duplicate names and undo.

prs.title: Undo and redo action definition edits from the Actions panel
prs.body:
Editing an action definition cannot currently be undone with Ctrl/Cmd+Z in the Actions panel.

Add bounded, transient action-definition undo/redo history and route Undo/Redo to it while Actions has focus. Restore reordering, deletion, renaming, recording/append, enabled-step changes, named calls and action shortcut bindings without changing document pixels or document History. Playback returns Undo routing to the document; undoing a completed recording does not restart recording.

Regression coverage includes definition restoration, pending recorded-step deletion, redo invalidation, enabled-step toggles and shell keyboard routing.

Validation on current main (614d0689): engine and UI `actions` tests pass.

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. Action-definition edits (record, stop, move, delete, toggle, rename) now push a snapshot of the action list, any pending recorded steps and the `actions.play:` shortcuts onto a separate bounded stack. `actions.undo` / `actions.redo` restore it without touching the document or the journal.

- Recording state is re-based on the current journal length, so undoing a pending-step deletion does not duplicate steps. Renames put the old function-key binding back.
- A new edit clears the redo stack, and undo is disabled while an action plays.
- The four engine tests and the shell test cover these cases, including the "document and journal unchanged" assertions.

Non-blocking: `actions.focused` is only cleared by a pointer press while the panel is drawn (or by `play`). If the panel is hidden by a keyboard shortcut after being clicked, Ctrl+Z would keep going to the action history.

prs.title: Read applied Sony RAW metadata and crop ILCE-6000 images
prs.body:
Older Sony ARWs can carry applied white balance and black levels only in encrypted SR2SubIFD metadata. PhotoCraft previously estimated WB from the scene and used a 512 black fallback, even when the file specified different levels. This change reads the observed common-key metadata with bounded allocation and checked offsets, keeps usable plain tags authoritative, and retains existing fallbacks for malformed metadata or other keys.

The measured ILCE-6000 image area now produces 6000 × 4000 images from its 6048 × 4024 sensor without overriding an explicit crop. Three measured files use their identical camera-applied WB instead of different grey-world estimates; full-resolution 16-bit ProPhoto-compatible development is retained. The pinned public RX0 fixture now asserts black 800 and applied WB. Sensor pixels continue through the RAW development pipeline.

Only the observed `11 22 33 44` key is supported. Metadata allocation is capped at 1 MiB and `Limits.max_alloc`; offsets, directory lengths and level values are checked. Synthetic regressions cover both byte orders, independent keystream observations, metadata precedence, invalid levels/gains, truncation, out-of-block offsets and allocation limits. The cipher data was independently recovered from black-box metadata observations; no sibling decoder implementation, camera colour table or dependency is included. See [the measurement and scope notes](https://github.com/optimalbytee/photocraft/blob/codex/sony-arw-metadata/docs/sony-arw-metadata.md).

Validation repeated after integration onto current upstream main (`79261615`):

- `cargo test -j 12 -p photocraft-raw --features corpus --locked`: 120 tests passed, including the SHA256-verified public RAW corpus.
- `cargo clippy -j 12 -p photocraft-raw --all-targets --features corpus --locked -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Changed Rust files pass formatting; layering passes for all 29 crates; `git diff --check` passes.

Additional evidence supplied with the handoff: 5 io RAW integration tests, wasm checks and all five applicable quick performance checks passed on the source commit. Three private ILCE-6000 files imported/exported as 6000 × 4000 RGB16 with a ProPhoto-compatible profile. Matched 24 MP release runs remained around 0.22 seconds per image across five rounds per version; this is a metadata/framing correction, with no speedup claim. The quick performance run used a different platform from its baseline and did not enforce full-size budgets.

Camera calibration and JPEG tone/DRO parity remain incomplete: PhotoCraft is still flatter/darker and less saturated than the camera JPEGs and LightCraft. This work is separate from the colour fitting in #2135 and camera profiles in #2230. Personal RAW/JPEG files and derived diagnostics are not included.

Related to #50. Informed by [LightCraft's Sony metadata investigation](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/535).

nodes.name: web build and wasm size gate

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. Sony ARWs whose plain tags lack a usable black level or white balance now fall back to the encrypted SR2SubIFD, and the ILCE-6000 gets its measured image area.

- The keystream recurrence in `decipher` is right: the ring slot holds k[n-127] and `(n-63) % 127` holds k[n-63], and the final incomplete word stays in the clear. Only the `11 22 33 44` key is accepted.
- `read` is bounded for hostile files: the length is capped at 1 MiB and `max_alloc`, the directory must fit inside the block, and value offsets are rebased so they cannot point outside the decrypted bytes. Only four SHORT/SSHORT values within 0..=16383 are taken. The truncation sweep and corrupted key, length and offset tests cover it.
- Precedence is sound: usable plain tags win, and a malformed plain white balance no longer hides a valid encrypted one. `sony_wb` now rejects non-finite and non-positive levels. Adding `s.crop == s.active` to the image-area lookup means a file's explicit crop wins, and a test covers it.

The branch conflicts with the base and needs a rebase. CI is green on this head, including the corpus tests.

prs.title: Draw right-to-left layer names in visual word order
prs.body: Fixes the word-order half of #1408 / #1693 / #1465 for layer names. Complements the font fallback PRs (#2758, #2646, #2836), which fix the tofu half. ## Why egui 0.36 shapes each font run with HarfRust, so an Arabic, Hebrew or Kurdish **word** draws right to left with its letters joined. What it lacks is paragraph bidi: a line's runs are placed left to right in logical order, so a layer named `سلام عليكم` shows as `عليكم سلام`. #2836 addresses this with `BidiInfo::reorder_line`. That reverses the characters too, and egui then reverses each word again. Each word ends up mirrored, joining forms come from the wrong neighbours, and the لا ligature is lost (measurements in my comment on #2836). ## What changes - **New `bidi_label::for_egui`.** It puts runs in visual order with the Unicode bidi algorithm (`visual_runs`) and leaves the letters of every stretch egui reverses by itself in logical order: - A right-to-left run is reversed, then each right-to-left-script stretch inside it is turned back. - Arabic-Indic digits inside a left-to-right run are pre-reversed. - **`layer_row_ui::truncated`**, which draws the names in Layers panel rows, uses it for names with right-to-left characters. - A long name is cut in **logical** order first, so it keeps its beginning and the "…" sits at its reading end. egui's own elision would keep the end of a reordered RTL name. - Galleys are cached by content, so unchanged rows don't re-layout. - **Other names lay out exactly as before.** - **New dependency:** `unicode-bidi = "0.3"`, already in the tree through usvg/resvg (MIT OR Apache-2.0). ## Screenshots Layers panel with this branch and #2758 (font fallback) merged locally, macOS. Before is `main` + #2758. / ## Tests - **String rules:** Arabic, Hebrew, Kurdish (Sorani), Persian with ZWNJ, European and Arabic-Indic digits, mixed Latin, and the UAX #9 W2 case (`Layer طبقة 2` → `Layer 2 طبقة`). - **With an Arabic or Hebrew system font installed** (skipped otherwise, like `font_preview`'s test), checks on what egui actually draws: - the first word's first letter has the larger x - `سلام` draws fewer glyphs than the mirrored `مالس`, so the لا ligature formed - a long name elides to fit, keeps its first word, and starts with "…" - `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm` and `cargo xtask scorecard --check` are clean. ## Limits - **Single-line painted labels only.** TextEdit, wrapped text and accessibility labels keep the logical string. - **Arabic-Indic digits written against Arabic letters with no space** (`طبقة١`) share one egui run with them and land on the wrong side. - **The Properties panel's layer-name header** uses a different path and is not covered yet. - **This is a stopgap until egui orders runs by bidi level** (emilk/egui#8577, which also fixes the RTL caret issue emilk/egui#8576). Delete `bidi_label` then. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. Arabic, Hebrew and other right-to-left layer names now draw with their words in visual order, and left-to-right text is returned untouched.

- `for_egui` reorders runs with the Unicode bidi algorithm and then un-reverses each stretch egui already reverses itself, so letters keep their joining forms and the lam-alef ligature. The tests pin word order, European and Arabic-Indic digits, Persian ZWNJ, and a glyph-position check that skips cleanly when no system font is present.
- `truncated_bidi` cuts the name in logical order by binary search and reorders afterwards, so a long name keeps its beginning and the ellipsis lands at the reading end. The left-to-right path is unchanged.
- The one dependency, `unicode-bidi`, is already in the lockfile.

prs.title: Scroll the viewport while outlining with Polygonal Lasso
prs.body: Polygonal Lasso now scrolls the canvas while the pointer rests near or just past an active viewport edge, including between vertex clicks with the button released. This lets a zoomed-in outline continue into an offscreen area without manually switching to navigation. Fixes #2231. Scrolling keeps placed vertices in document coordinates, uses the existing rotated, mirrored and pixel-aspect-aware view mapping and Overscroll bounds, and requests further frames for a stationary pointer. Returning to the interior, opening a dialog or using temporary navigation stops automatic motion. An unfinished polygon is tied to its starting document so switching documents or tools cannot later commit it to a different document. Shift-constrained segments remain supported while the view scrolls. Validation on `ebf3777aec961d1815aa141d9987eaa645c2273f`: - All 22 Polygonal Lasso tests passed, including the new rotation/mirroring/pixel-aspect/Shift regression. Coverage includes all edges and corners, stationary button-up continuation, unchanged vertices and history, next-click mapping, one-step commit/undo, modal and temporary navigation, inactive panes, document/tool changes, Escape and Overscroll-off boundaries. - Native UI library: 2,931 passed, 13 ignored, 0 failed. - Native offscreen replay: 60 stationary button-up frames moved the view center from `[180, 150]` to `[313.7499, 150]`, revealed the blue marker, and retained both document-space vertices. Before/after renders were inspected. - [Hosted CI run 38754718916](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38754718916) passed on this exact head: Ubuntu and Windows workspace tests with HEIF; Ubuntu without-HEIF and craft-fonts suites; strict workspace/all-target Clippy; dependency layering; scorecard verification; corpus tests; L0–L6 Wasm checks; and browser release build/size gate. The workflow intentionally skipped fuzzing. Before: After:

approval.body:
Approving. I read the whole diff at ebf3777a.

- `polygon_edge_scroll` only moves the view center. Placed vertices stay in document coordinates, and the scroll goes through `ViewXform::unmap_vec` with the view's flip, rotation and pixel aspect, then through the existing Overscroll clamp, so the displayed axes and Overscroll-off bounds are respected. Inputs are guarded (finite pointer, `dt` and zoom, a positive edge band, delta time capped at 50 ms).
- It does not run while a dialog, popup, text edit, Camera Raw, a drag or temporary navigation (Space or middle button) is active, when the window is unfocused, or when the pointer is over the other tiled pane, and it only runs for the active document in the primary view.
- `polygon_cancel_stale` now also drops an unfinished polygon when the tool is no longer Polygonal Lasso, and `polygon_doc` is cleared on retract, commit and Escape, so an outline cannot be committed to another document.
- The new tests cover all eight edges and corners with flip and rotation, button-up continuation with unchanged vertices and history, the next click using the panned transform with a single undo step, pixel aspect and Shift-constrained segments after panning, Overscroll off, dialog/Space/middle-button pauses, the inactive pane, and document and tool switches. The only harness change is rendering dialogs, which the dialog test needs.
- No new user-visible strings, so no catalog changes are needed.

prs.title: feat(actions): import and export reusable Actions JSON files
prs.body:
## Summary

Partially addresses #1951.

PhotoCraft persists recorded actions internally, but users
cannot conveniently export their action libraries or import
actions from another installation.

This adds JSON import/export through the engine commands `actions.import` and `actions.export`, using PhotoCraft's existing versioned ActionsFile format. The Actions panel, CLI, and MCP share the engine implementation.

## Changes

### Actions Panel

Add an Actions menu containing:

- Load Actions… (supports JSON alongside the existing ATN path)
- Save Actions… (.json)

The panel keeps file selection and status messages; merge, rename, validation, nested-reference retargeting, and serialization run in the engine. Menu labels and status strings are translated.

### Export

- Export the current action library as JSON.
- Use the existing ActionsFile version 1 format.
- Preserve action names, commands, parameters, and order.
- Enforce the existing 16 MiB Actions file limit.
- Report successful exports through the status system.

### Import

- Read versioned Actions JSON files.
- Preserve existing actions.
- Append new actions to the library.
- Skip already imported identical actions.
- Rename conflicting imports using `(Imported N)`.
- Retarget nested action references after renaming.
- Support nested references by action name or imported index.
- Update the action-library revision for persistence.
- Prevent imports while actions are recording or playing.

### File Validation

Reject:

- Invalid JSON.
- Unsupported file versions.
- Files exceeding the 16 MiB limit.
- Empty or duplicate action names.
- Excessively long action names.
- More than 1,024 imported actions.
- More than 10,000 steps per action.
- Invalid nested action indexes.

### Regression Tests

Added tests for:

- Export/import round-trip preservation.
- Repeated imports without creating duplicates.
- Duplicate-name handling.
- Nested action reference preservation.
- Invalid JSON and unsupported versions.
- Duplicate action names.
- Import rejection during recording.
- Existing action preservation after failed imports.

## Compatibility

This uses PhotoCraft's native JSON Actions format.

It does not add Photoshop `.atn` import support.

## Files Changed

- crates/ui-egui/src/actions.rs

## Validation

Completed:
- Four commits pushed to an isolated branch.
- Source-level implementation review.
- Regression tests added.
- Remote branch verification.
- Duplicate contribution screening.

Pending:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui
- Native file picker verification
- Browser import/export verification
- Persistence regression testing
- Upstream CI

Tests have not been executed.

## Issue

Partially addresses #1951.

The Play-button behavior is handled in a separate PR.

approval.body:
Read the whole diff. `actions.import` and `actions.export` add a version 1 Actions JSON file, with Load Actions taking `.json` as well as `.atn` and a "Save Actions… (.json)" menu entry.

- Import is validated before anything changes: version, at most 1024 actions and 10,000 steps, unique non-empty names within 256 bytes, in-range disabled and dialog indices, and a 16 MiB cap. Nested `actions.play` calls by name or index are retargeted, and a bad index fails the whole import.
- Name clashes become "Name (Imported N)" and the suffix is cut on a char boundary within 256 bytes. Identical actions are reused, so a re-import is a no-op, and the dependency loop is bounded.
- Both commands refuse to run while recording or playing, and `actions.export` with a `path` is now treated as an ambient path in the workspace authorizer, with a test.
- No new `tl!` strings: the new menu entry reuses "Save Actions…".
